title: Which record owns the scan of STEGO's own Go modules for known vulnerabilities?
description: The workflows check STEGO's own dependencies: go mod verify and govulncheck in checks.yml and runtime-library.yml, and vulnerability-scan.yml (ST-ASR-TOOL06), which scans every Go module on main each week. No design record asks for this, so no test of it can be a proof: the test of the module list in scripts/test_release_publishing.py names no record. Options: (a) a new rule of ST-STD-TRUST: every Go module of STEGO MUST be verified against its go.sum and scanned for known vulnerabilities by each check of the module and on main each week, and a reachable known vulnerability MUST fail the check; its test is the module list test; (b) a UC requirement of an Assuring use case; (c) keep it as tooling with no proof. Recommendation: (a): it is an engineering rule for STEGO's own code, as the rules of ST-STD-TRUST are, and it holds the scan to every module, also one added later.

title: Where does stego build download take the runtime pin of a service, while the runtime library is not released on the public module proxy?
description: Since the archetype move (ST-SUP-RC20-OC39) every generated service imports the runtime library, and the examples do too. stego deps and local builds resolve the pin from the common registry's runtime folder, verified by the pinned hash (ST-SUP-INV10). stego build download runs in a fixed environment with the public module proxy only, and a module that the proxy cannot supply stops it (ST-BLD-UC02-R03). The runtime is not released: no tag registry/runtime/<version> is pushed and stego.dev serves no go-import page for it, so the application build job of CI stops at github.com/jsell-rh/stego/registry/runtime v0.30.0. Options: (a) the Product owner releases the runtime at each pin: serve the go-import page, push the tag registry/runtime/<version> at the commit whose folder hashes to the pin, and the public proxy then supplies it; (b) stego build download takes the pin from the common registry's runtime folder as stego deps does, as a local file proxy before the public proxy, only when the folder hashes to the pinned sum, and the build record names that source; (c) the application build job builds a service that does not import the runtime until (a). Recommendation: (b) now, because the zip is verified by the pinned hash and so is the same bytes as a release, with (a) at the first release; the build record names the source, so a reviewer sees which builds did not use the public proxy.

title: Can stego build download take the runtime pin from the runtime folder of a STEGO checkout that a flag names, for a source with no runtime folder?
description: Developer walkthrough of 2026-11-13, step 25 (F7): a user project holds no registry/runtime folder, and origin has no registry/runtime/<version> tag, so stego build download cannot get the runtime pin and a clean machine cannot build a generated service. The Product owner chose both remedies: (a) the owner pushes the tags of agents/followup/tag-plan.md, and (b) stego build download takes a flag that names the runtime folder of a STEGO checkout. ST-BLD-UC02-R05 and ST-BLD-CLI02 name only the runtime folder of the source revision. The follow-up worker built (b) as --runtime-folder <folder>: the folder passes every check of R05 (go.sum, the pin that the binary carries, sum.golang.org, no link or special file), and the cache and build records name it as checkout:registry/runtime; it is refused for a source that holds its own runtime folder, for a go.mod with no runtime pin, and for a folder with no go.mod. Proposed restatement of R05, for the owner: When go.mod requires the runtime library and the source revision holds the common registry's runtime folder registry/runtime, or the author names the runtime folder of a STEGO checkout for a source that holds none, the download MUST take that version from that folder only after ... (the rest as today), and the records MUST name which folder supplied it. Proposed addition to ST-BLD-CLI02: [--runtime-folder <stego checkout>/registry/runtime]. Tests ST-BLD-UC02-R05-T10 to T12 prove (b) under R05 until the owner restates it. Decision (orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-13): the proposed restatement is accepted. ST-BLD-UC02-R05 and ST-BLD-CLI02 are restated to name --runtime-folder.

title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Research of core3 (2026-11-17, origin/main 0f75423d): stego init of rest-crud passes stego validate as written. The scaffold of rpc-service (now grpc-application with command and query, ST-SUP-RC07-OC19) is refused one fault at a time: first proto_files (1 to 128); with a proto file and no method, grpc-application refuses a service with no entity, command or query (ST-SUP-Q101); with an entity, postgres-adapter needs schema_generation. With a declared method, ST-DECL-INV75 now also needs a command or query on it, and so a fill. The scaffold of browser-service is refused for api_prefix, then for routes (1 to 64). So the smallest accepted content of rpc-service is a proto file with one unary method, one query on it with its fill, and the settings base_path, error_type_base and postgres-adapter schema_generation; of browser-service, api_prefix and one route. Prior art: cargo new, go mod init with gonew templates, rails new, kubebuilder init and helm create each write a project that builds and runs as written, from a template that is versioned with the tool or the template repository, and CI of the tool builds each template; buf and protoc plugins ship a minimal .proto with one service and one method. None asks the author to fill required values before the first build; values that only the deployment has (connection strings, issuers) are environment, not project. Options: (a) the Archetype (ST-SUP-EN03) gets an example content field: files under the archetype folder (a proto file, a fill) and the declaration text that init writes, with the service name and module path as placeholders; a component schema marks each setting the declaration must give (author supplied), so that init --empty names them and checking refuses their absence by name; a test inits, validates and builds every archetype of the registry. (b) the example content lives in Declaring's code, one case per archetype. (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a). It follows the prior art (the template is versioned with what it scaffolds), it needs no change to STEGO's code when an archetype changes, and the test of every archetype stops a registry change that breaks its scaffold. The author-supplied mark is also what R05 needs: today a schema marks as required both settings the declaration gives and settings only the running service gets (connection_string of postgres-adapter, issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell them apart. Until a decision, UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated for rpc-service and browser-service. Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-17: the Archetype gets example content (files and the declaration text that init writes, with the service name and module path as placeholders); a component schema marks each setting the declaration must give (author supplied); a test inits, validates and builds every archetype of the registry.

title: May a field that a finished rename named be renamed again?
description: ST-GEN-UC12-R04-T02 (owner decision of 2026-11-06, Q5) renames Note.title to heading with its expand and contract steps, and then heading to headline with its expand step. ST-DECL-INV58 requires the entity to declare the Field of each rename, so checking refuses the finished rename note-title-rename once the second rename gives the field the name headline: 'the entity does not declare the field, which a rename names by its name after the change'. ST-GEN-UC15-R03 keeps a finished change in the declaration until a new baseline folds it, so the second rename can never be declared. Options: (a) restate ST-DECL-INV58 so that the Field of a rename may be the From of a later rename of the same entity, in the order of the schema history, and only the last name of the chain must be declared; (b) refuse a second rename of a field until a new baseline (ST-GEN-UC10) folds the first, and restate ST-GEN-UC12-R04-T02 to a rename after a fold. Recommendation: (a), which keeps Q5 and needs only the check of the chain in checking; the generator and the API name rule already follow the chain. ST-GEN-UC12-R04-T02 is written in cmd/stego/schema_step_plan_test.go and stays not automated until this is decided. Written by the schema-change builder, 2026-11-14.

title: May a declaration mark a timestamp field as one that the client sets?
description: Finding G2 of the walkthrough re-run (2026-11-14). ST-SUP-RC20-OC17 makes every timestamp field server-managed: a create, update or upsert clears the client value and sets the time of the request. So a declaration cannot hold a date that the client chooses, such as the due date due_at of a task: the create stores the time of the request, and a PUT keeps the stored value. Options: (A) keep every timestamp server-managed; a client date is declared as a string field with a format; (B) add a field setting, such as client_set: true, that a timestamp field may state: the client then sets it in a create, an update, an upsert and a patch (it is patchable), it is an RFC 3339 time that the generated code checks and stores in UTC, and it stays out of the server-managed fields of OC17; a timestamp without the setting stays server-managed, so no declaration changes meaning; (C) make a timestamp client-set by default, and server-managed only for the names created_time and updated_time or a computed field, which changes the meaning of existing declarations. Recommendation: B, because a due date is a common need, the default stays safe, and the declaration states the choice in one place. Decided by the Product owner, 2026-11-14: an opt-in field setting client_set: true lets the client send a timestamp value (option B above; the owner's decision names it (a)). Server-managed stays the default, so created_at and updated_at cannot be forged: a declaration that marks them, created_time, updated_time, a computed field or a field that is not a timestamp client_set is refused. Built in the declaration, the rest-api decode and its check of the value (an RFC 3339 time, answered in UTC), and the OpenAPI document.

title: Against which shape of its field are the values of a relax, and the field of an add or a relax, checked when a later step changes the same field?
description: Found while building the relax kind (decision on F12, owner, 2026-11-13). ST-DECL-INV58 checks the field of a schema change against the entity as the head declares it, and ST-DECL-INV62 now checks the Definition of a relax against the field as it left it, with each later relax of the same field undone (types.FieldAfterRelax). Two cases are still refused although the history is sound: (1) a relax or an add of a field that a later rename renames, because the field no longer has the name that the change names; and (2) a relax of a field that a later retype or require changes, because the relax is checked against the retyped field. Also, ST-DECL-INV60 takes an add as open for ever, so a rename of a field that an add added is refused for ever. Options: (a) check each change against the shape at its own step, every later step undone as gen.Context.AtSchemaStep undoes them, once the undo of retype and require is built (builder 2b), and take add and relax as finished at their expand step for ST-DECL-INV60; (b) keep the present rules and document that a field changes by at most one of rename, retype or require after a relax or an add; (c) let the author fold the history (ST-GEN-UC10) before such a change. Recommendation: (a), in the change that builds the undo of retype and require, with (b) documented until then. Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14; built in the follow-up fu-q17 (ST-DECL-INV58, ST-DECL-INV60, ST-DECL-INV62, ST-DECL-INV63 restated).

title: Does a slot have inputs that a slot binding gives, or does the no-bypass rule hold for component settings only until one exists?
description: ST-DECL-SP07, ST-DECL-INV24, ST-DECL-UC06-R03 and ST-SUP-UC01-R07 refuse a value for 'a setting or a slot input' that its component's schema marks as a bypass. The Config schema of a Component (ST-SUP-EN09) can carry the mark (design input 01 adds it to the field's meaning). But no slot has inputs: the Slot (ST-SUP-EN08) has name, component, contract, phase and operations, and the Slot binding (ST-DECL-EN05) has collection, slot, operator, fills, runs as, audit annotations and relationships written. A binding that writes any other key is refused by strict reading (ST-DECL-INV02), so no binding can give a slot input a value today. ST-DECL-SP07 is the last missing builder of ST-DECL-QRY01, so 36 records of Declaring (all of ST-DECL-UC04 to UC09, and UC10-R01) are not built until it is. Options: (a) the rule holds for component settings now, and for slot inputs vacuously, because a slot declares none; the builder builds ST-DECL-SP07 over the marked settings, and changes the test records SP07-T, INV24-T and UC06-R03-T01 to drop the slot input case until a slot input exists; a later change that adds slot inputs adds their arm with them. (b) add an Inputs field to the Slot (each input with its type and a bypass mark) and to the Slot binding (the values it gives), so the fixtures of the test records can be written as they are; this adds a new part to the declaration format and to every slot contract. Recommendation: (a). No component and no fill needs a slot input today, and (a) closes the rule for every value a declaration can give. Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-17: the no-bypass rule holds for component settings now, and for slot inputs vacuously, because a slot declares none; ST-DECL-SP07 is built over the marked settings, and a later change that adds slot inputs adds their arm with them.

title: Must a reference to an entity under the same ancestor stay under that ancestor, and where is the rule held?
description: Found by the sixth walkthrough (N10), 2026-11-17. A ticket of project WEB was created with the sprint of project CORE (201). References are decided by permission only (ST-SUP-RP10-LC05, ST-DECL-INV85), and no record states that a reference shares the scope of its row: ST-DECL-EN04 gives a collection its scope, and ST-SUP-RC20-OC24 checks only the path. Options: (a) no rule, and the docs tell a fill to check it; (b) every reference between two entities under the same ancestor must share it; (c) a reference declares within: <field>, the field that the row and the referenced row must have equal, which checking refuses when it is not well formed, and which the write enforces: the runtime before the statement, with a clear 400, and the database with a composite foreign key; within: none states that a reference across the ancestor is intended. Recommendation: (c), with a checking warning for a reference between two entities that both refer to the same ancestor entity and declare no within. (b) is too strong: Jira and GitHub link issues across projects on purpose. (a) fails as Rails belongs_to fails in multi-tenant applications: the model checks the ID only, and a second write path, a race or a fill skips the check. Citus and django-multitenant put the tenant column in each foreign key, so the database holds the rule for every writer; STEGO already keys each table by (tenant_id, id), so the key (tenant_id, <within>, <reference>) is the same method one level down. So the rule is both: checking holds the shape, and the write holds the data. Decision: the recommendation, decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17. ST-DECL-EN02 References gets within, ST-DECL-INV93 checks it, ST-SUP-RP10-LC37 refuses a write that breaks it, and ST-SUP-RC01-OC46 emits the composite key.

title: May a service name start with a digit?
description: Found by core4 in PR 403, 2026-11-17. ST-DECL-INV86 lets the service name start with a digit, because stego init names the service after its folder. But a project folder 001 gives a service that cannot run: the tenancy generator derives the roles 001_runtime and 001_owner, which are not plain PostgreSQL names, and refuses them only at apply; and the generated Kubernetes Service is named 001, which Kubernetes refuses, since a Service name is a DNS-1035 label that starts with a letter. Options: (a) the service name MUST start with a letter (^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$), and stego init refuses a folder name that starts with a digit, with the form and the step to rename the folder; (b) keep the form, and derive each name that must start with a letter with a fixed prefix, such as s001_runtime and the Service s-001; (c) keep the form, and add stego init --name so that the author names the service apart from the folder. Recommendation: (a). It matches the strictest name the service name becomes (Kubernetes Service names, DNS-1035; PostgreSQL unquoted identifiers), as Helm release names and Knative service names do (DNS-1035, letter first). (b) hides a second name that operators see in the database and the cluster but not in the declaration; Kubernetes itself moved Service names from DNS-1123 to DNS-1035 for this reason. (c) can come later and does not fix a declaration written by hand. A declaration whose service name starts with a digit cannot have reached a running service, so (a) breaks none. Decision: (a), decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17: the service name starts with a letter (DNS-1035, as Kubernetes Service names need).

title: What does 'a secret field MUST NOT be stored' mean for a field that the service must read again?
description: Found by walkthrough 10 (rank 3), 2026-11-18. ST-DECL-UC05-R06 says that a field of sensitivity secret MUST NOT be stored, and its test ST-DECL-UC05-R06-T02 is not automated yet. The generated service stores a secret field in clear in its table, and ST-DECL-EN03 gives no rule for its storage. Thus a person who can read the table, a backup or a replica reads each secret. Prior art: Rails 7 Active Record Encryption (encrypts :token) encrypts one column with AES-256-GCM, with keys from the credentials, a list of earlier keys for rotation, and a deterministic mode only for a column that must be found by value. Laravel has the encrypted cast, and Django has no built-in field encryption. Google Tink and the AWS Database Encryption SDK give AEAD encryption with associated data, so a ciphertext copied to another row or column does not decrypt. HashiCorp Vault Transit encrypts with a key that never leaves Vault. PostgreSQL pgcrypto encrypts in SQL, but the key is then in the statement, the server log and pg_stat_statements. Transparent data encryption and disk encryption protect only against a stolen disk, not against a SQL reader or a backup. A secret that the service only compares, such as an API key that a client sends, is stored as a slow hash (Argon2id, OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet) or an HMAC with a server key. Known failures: the key in the same database or the same backup as the data; deterministic encryption that tells which rows hold the same value; encryption with no associated data, so ciphertexts can be swapped between rows; keys that are never rotated; the plain value in logs, audit rows, events or error texts. Options: (a) encryption at rest per field: the generated code encrypts each secret field with AES-256-GCM before it writes it and decrypts it after it reads it, with the associated data tenant, table, row ID and column, and a key ring from the environment (a secret need of the service with the current key and the earlier keys); the field is never in a list filter, a sort, a unique key or an index, and never in an audit row, an event, a log or a problem; (b) a write-only secret: the service stores only an HMAC-SHA-256 or Argon2id hash and never gives the value back, for a secret that is only compared; (c) a database-level concern: change ST-DECL-UC05-R06 to say that a secret is never in a log, an audit row, an event or a response, and that its storage at rest is the encryption of the database and of its backups, which the operator gives; (d) refuse the sensitivity secret on an entity field: a secret belongs in a secret store, and the field holds only its name. Recommendation: (a), with (b) as a declared form for a secret that is only compared (such as hash: true on the field), because R06 already promises that a secret is not stored in clear, and a database-level rule (c) does not protect against a reader of the table or a backup. (a) needs a rule on ST-DECL-EN03 (a secret field cannot be a key, an index, a search field or a sort field), an output contract on postgres-adapter and rest-api, and a key ring secret need; it does not block the current walkthroughs. Decision: (a) with (b) as a declared form, Product owner, 2026-11-18. A secret field is encrypted at rest, per field, with AES-256-GCM: the associated data is the table, the column, the row ID and the tenant, so that a ciphertext does not decrypt in another row, column or tenant. The key ring comes from the environment as a secret file, for the api and worker pods only. A compare-only secret (compare_only: true), which the service only checks and never reads back, such as a PIN or a recovery code, is stored as an Argon2id hash. Thus the generated code meets ST-DECL-UC05-R06: no secret is stored in clear. A secret field is never a key, an index, a list filter or a sort field: no deterministic index (ST-DECL-INV101). Prior art: Rails 7 encryption (deterministic and non-deterministic modes), Tink AEAD and key sets, Vault Transit, and the key commitment of the AWS Encryption SDK. Known failures that the design avoids: pgcrypto keys in SQL logs, nonce reuse in GCM, no key rotation, and no way to re-encrypt. The design: ST-DECL-EN03 fields 5 and 8, ST-DECL-INV101, ST-SUP-RP16, ST-SUP-RP10-LC44 to LC46, ST-SUP-RP14-LC12, ST-SUP-RC01-OC48 and OC49, ST-SUP-RC20-OC48, ST-SUP-RC32-OC20 and OC21, ST-SUP-RC33-OC13.

title: How does a declaration keep a field that only a command changes out of a CRUD update?
description: Found by walkthrough 6 (U3), and open in walkthroughs 7, 8 and 9. A CRUD PUT can set status archived (run 6) or active (run 8), and thus skip the refusals of the commands move-ticket and activate-product that guard that field. The collection setting patchable limits the fields of a patch, but no setting limits the fields of an update or an upsert, and ST-SUP-RC20-OC17 makes only computed, timestamp and audit fields server-managed. Prior art: Kubernetes splits an object into spec and status, and a client writes status only through the subresource /status, which has its own permission. AIP-203 marks a field OUTPUT_ONLY (the server ignores a client value) or IMMUTABLE (a changed value on update is INVALID_ARGUMENT). OpenAPI has readOnly. Rails attr_readonly ignored a change in silence, and Rails 7.1 added raise_on_assign_to_attr_readonly because the silence hid faults; Django REST framework has read_only_fields, which it ignores in silence. Options: (a) a field setting writable with the values always (the default), create (the field is set on a create and then only by a command or a worker) and never (only a command or a worker sets it; a create takes its declared default): an update, an upsert or a patch that gives another value than the stored one gets 400 that names the field, and a body that leaves it out keeps the stored value; (b) a collection setting updatable, a list of the fields that an update and an upsert may change, as patchable is for a patch; (c) a warning at checking for each field that a command of the entity writes and that a CRUD update may also change; (d) no change: an author who needs the guard removes update from the collection or adds a before_update gate. Recommendation: (a). It states the rule once on the field, so every collection, the OpenAPI document (readOnly) and the TypeScript and Go SDKs agree, and it refuses in place of a silent ignore, as Rails 7.1 and AIP-203 IMMUTABLE do and as rest-api 4.7.0 does for the scope field of a scoped collection. It needs a field setting on ST-DECL-EN03, a declaration invariant, and output contracts on rest-api for the update, the upsert, the patch and the OpenAPI document. Decision: (a), decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-18: a field setting writable with the values always (the default), create and never; ST-DECL-INV100 holds the declaration to it, and the rest-api output contracts ST-SUP-RC20-OC44 to OC47 refuse a write that changes such a field and mark it readOnly in the OpenAPI document.

title: Is a field declared sensitivity: public the same as a field with no sensitivity, for the search of a list, its order and its search index?
description: Found while fixing walkthrough 15, W15-B1, 2026-11-19. fills.md and types.Field say that sensitivity is public, pii or secret, and that the default is public. But the generators read a public field by its empty sensitivity: postgresadapter.Searchable gives a search index only to a field with no sensitivity, restapi.searchKind lets a list search only such a field, and the list order takes only such a field. So a field written sensitivity: public, which the docs call the same as the default, gets no search, no order and no search index. No declaration in the examples, the docs or the walkthroughs writes sensitivity: public, so no service is known to have it. The W15-B1 fix changes only the seal: a seal from public is undone as a field with no sensitivity, so the seal keeps the search index of a base that wrote no sensitivity (the usual case); a base that wrote sensitivity: public on a field that a list searches is then refused by the index check of ST-GEN-INV33, fail closed. Prior art: a default value of an enum setting means the same as the value written out (Kubernetes API conventions: defaulted fields, OpenAPI default), and a linter, not the meaning, prefers one form (yamllint, kube-linter). Options: (a) public and no sensitivity mean the same everywhere: the generators read a field as public when its sensitivity is empty or public, so a field written public gets the search, the order and the search index; this changes 001_initial of a service whose base writes sensitivity: public on a searched field of a listed entity, so the check against the base must refuse that head with a fault that names the field and the remedy (write no sensitivity, or keep the release), or the change must wait for a new schema_generation; (b) validation refuses sensitivity: public and names the remedy, leave it out, so one form remains; a base that has it can no longer be built, which needs the same remedy; (c) keep the generators as they are and document that sensitivity: public turns off the search, the order and the search index of the field. Recommendation: (a), with the refusal of the check against the base for a base that writes public on a searched field of a listed entity, because the docs and the type already say that public is the default, and (c) makes a field that a reader takes as public behave as pii.

title: How does a registry component state the needs that the platform requirements are derived from?
description: Finding N8 of the walkthrough re-run (2026-11-14): apply writes no platform requirements. ST-DLV-UC01-R01, ST-DLV-INV01, ST-DLV-DS01 and ST-GEN-CLI01 say that the platform requirements come from the needs that the service's components state, and ST-DLV-TD01 and ST-DLV-UC01-R02-T02 say that a component in the registry copy states a need (postgres-adapter states the secret orders-database). But the component record ST-SUP-EN09 has no field for needs, no record gives the shape of a need for each of the nine kinds of ST-VO53, and no component.yaml states a need. The names of TD01 (orders-database, orders-db, order-events) also hold the service name, so a need name must come in part from the declaration. Options: (A) add a field Platform needs to ST-SUP-EN09: a needs list in component.yaml, each entry with a kind of ST-VO53, a name, and only the shape fields of its kind (secret: keys; configuration: none; backing store: engine; topic: none; identity issuer: none; ingress: port; egress: port; cluster permission: API group, resource and verbs; pod security: level). A name may hold the service name and the value of a setting of the component that the declaration gives, and nothing else. The registry decodes it strictly and refuses an unknown field, so a host name, an address or a secret value has no place to go (ST-DLV-INV02); apply refuses a resolved value that holds one. (B) derive the needs from the generated code (the environment variables and ports it reads): no registry change, but a need then depends on code, which the goal of ST-DLV-UC01 and ST-DLV-UC01-R05-T03 forbid. (C) the declaration states the needs per component: the author must restate what every component needs, against INV01. Recommendation: A. It is the only option that keeps the needs in the registry and the declaration alone, and the strict shape per kind makes ST-DLV-UC01-R02 a schema rule. Until it is decided, ST-DLV-UC01 is stopped, and with it ST-DLV-UC02 (its fixture ST-DLV-TD02 is the file that apply writes) and the platform edges of the architecture view (ST-GEN-UC08-R01-T01). Decided (A) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: component.yaml gets a strictly parsed needs list, each entry with a kind of ST-VO53, a name and only the shape fields of its kind. A need name may hold only the service name and the settings that the declaration gives, so an environment value has no place to go (ST-DLV-INV02). It goes into the field Platform needs of ST-SUP-EN09.

title: What is the shape of the environment file that stego env check reads, and who owns its schema?
description: Finding N8 of the walkthrough re-run (2026-11-14): stego env check (ST-DLV-CLI02) is an unknown command. ST-DLV-DS02 says that each value must be of the type that the environment schema states, such as an image named by digest, and ST-DLV-TM02 says that the environment file is the platform's typed file for one service in one environment. But no record gives that schema: which sections the file has, how a value names its requirement, and which type each kind takes. ST-DLV-TD02 puts secret values (the canary text) in the file, and ST-DLV-EN05 says that the ApplicationSet reads from each environment file a destination cluster, namespace and overlay path, so the file also carries those. Options: (A) STEGO owns a versioned schema for the file, and the check decodes it strictly with a size limit: one YAML file with schema version 1, the service, the environment, the image as repository@sha256 digest, the destination (cluster, namespace, overlay path), and one section per requirement kind of ST-VO53 keyed by the requirement name (a secret with its keys, whose values the check skips and never shows; an egress with an address and a port number from 1 to 65535; and so on). An unknown field is an unknown shape (ST-DLV-UC02-R04-T03), and a name that no requirement names is listed as unused (ST-DLV-UC02-R05). (B) the check reads the platform's own files (the overlay, its Secret and ConfigMap manifests): no new format, but more files, secret manifests read in full, and no one place for the types. (C) the platform writes its own schema and the check takes it as input: the types are then not STEGO's to prove. Recommendation: A. The records name one file and one environment schema, the platform keeps the file in its own repository, and a STEGO-owned schema lets the check prove the type rules of ST-DLV-UC02-R02. Until it is decided, ST-DLV-UC02 is stopped. Decided (A) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: STEGO owns a versioned YAML environment schema with strict parsing and a size limit. The file holds the image by sha256 digest, the destination (cluster, namespace and overlay path) and one section per requirement kind. The check skips secret values and never shows them. It goes into ST-DLV-TM02.

title: How does the fill change of ST-DLV-UC01-R05-T03 read an environment variable when a fill may not import os?
description: Found by the Delivering builder, 2026-11-14. ST-DLV-UC01-R05-T03 says that a fill of the service gets a new call that reads the environment variable EXTRA_TOKEN, and that the next apply leaves the platform requirements byte-identical. But a bound fill must be qualified before apply accepts it, and qualification refuses a fill that imports os: the fill allow list of the standard library (ST-EXT-UC01-R03) holds no package that reads the environment. So the step cannot be written as recorded. The other steps of the test (the declaration takes out the Kafka producer, the registry copy adds the key sslmode) are written in the builder's notes and wait for this decision; every other test of ST-DLV-UC01 is automated. Options: (A) the fill change is a new call that names EXTRA_TOKEN without reading the environment, such as a constant or a log field with that name, which still catches a derivation that scans the code of the service for environment variable names; (B) the step changes an unbound fill in the fills folder, which may import os because no binding qualifies it; (C) the step is taken out, because the fill allow list already keeps a fill from reading the environment, and the step of the registry and the declaration proves the rest. Recommendation: A. It keeps a qualified, bound fill, so apply reads it as it reads every fill of the service, and the name EXTRA_TOKEN is in the code that a wrong derivation would read. Until it is decided, ST-DLV-UC01-R05-T03 stays not automated yet. Decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: (A). The fill change of ST-DLV-UC01-R05-T03 is a new call that only names EXTRA_TOKEN and does not read the environment, so the fill stays qualified and bound.

title: Must the environment check refuse a url value that is not an HTTPS URL?
description: The third walkthrough (2026-11-15, G5) found that stego env check passes STEGO_AUTHN_KEYS_URL: ftp://... ST-VO63-C01 says only that a url is a url, but every url variable of the shipped registry is an HTTPS URL by its description (key sets, issuers, the audit sink, the collector, the browser origins). Options: (A) the check refuses each url value whose scheme is not https; (B) a variable states its allowed schemes, a new fact of ST-SUP-EN14, and the check holds the value to them; (C) the check holds a url value only to an absolute URL. Recommendation: A now, as no shipped variable takes another scheme, and B when one does. Built as A, the safe behaviour, until it is decided (walkthrough-3 fixes, PR B).

title: How does the variable list state that one of two variables, such as DATABASE_URL or DATABASE_URL_FILE, is required?
description: The third walkthrough (2026-11-15, G6) found that each database URL of the variable list is required: false, with the text that the process does not start when the variable and its _FILE form have no value. The rule is only prose, so stego env check passes a file that gives neither. The secret and backing store needs of postgres-adapter now make the check fail for a file with no database, but the check still does not see a missing role URL. Options: (A) a variable states one_of with the name of its other form, the platform requirements hold it, and the check needs one of the two; (B) each such pair becomes one secret need with a key per role, and the variables stay optional; (C) keep the prose. Recommendation: A, as it keeps the variable list the one source of what the process reads. Not built: it changes the facts of ST-SUP-EN14 and of the platform requirements (walkthrough-3 fixes, PR B). Decided (A) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-15: ST-SUP-EN14 gets a field One of, a group name. The variables of one group are a pair, and the process needs exactly one of them, such as DATABASE_URL or DATABASE_URL_FILE. The registry refuses a group with fewer than two variables, with variables of two components, or with a variable that is required on its own. The platform requirements carry the group (ST-DLV-EN08), stego env check fails when the environment file gives no variable of a group a value, or more than one, and deploy/environment-variables.md shows the group. A secret variable with a secret source counts as given when the file gives its Secret with its key. Built as ST-SUP-EN14 field One of, ST-DLV-EN08 field One of, ST-SUP-INV24, ST-SUP-UC01-R09, ST-DLV-UC01-R06, ST-DLV-UC01-R07 and ST-DLV-UC02-R06.

title: What fields does the delivery stanza of a declaration have, and where does each one go?
description: Found by the Delivering builder, 2026-11-15, for finding N8b of the third walkthrough. ST-DLV-UC06, ST-DLV-UC07, ST-DLV-PO04, ST-GEN-CLI01 and ST-DLV-TD01 say that the declaration has a delivery stanza that names the CI provider, the Argo CD project and the location of the platform's environment files. But the Declaration ST-DECL-EN01 has no field for it, no record gives its shape, and the declaration parser refuses the field delivery as not declared. The ApplicationSet of ST-DLV-UC07-R04 also must name the base, which is in the service's own repository; no record says where the repository address comes from, and the compiler does not read the Git remote. Options: (A) add an optional field Delivery stanza to ST-DECL-EN01, decoded strictly: delivery.ci is the CI provider of ST-VO51 (github-actions or konflux); delivery.argocd.project is the Argo CD project; delivery.argocd.source is the address of the service's repository and the revision that the ApplicationSet reads the base from; delivery.argocd.environments is the repository, the revision and the path pattern of the platform's environment files. Every other field, such as a cluster, a namespace, an overlay, a pipeline reference or a signer, is refused with its path (ST-DLV-UC07-R04-T02, ST-DLV-UC04-R01-T02). Without delivery.argocd, apply writes no ApplicationSet; without delivery.ci, it writes no CI file. (B) The same fields, but as settings of the components ci-pipeline and a new argocd component in the overrides of the declaration, so that the component schema (ST-SUP-EN09 field 5) checks them. (C) The stanza names the provider only; the project is the service name, and the registry names one platform repository and one path pattern for the environment files of every service. Recommendation: A. The records name one stanza in the declaration, and a strict stanza with only these fields keeps every environment value out, because a field for it does not exist. Until it is decided, ST-DLV-UC07-R04 and ST-DLV-UC06-R01 are stopped. The Kubernetes base (ST-DLV-UC07-R01 to R03) and the plan line of ST-DLV-UC07-R05 do not need it and are built. Decided (A) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-15: the declaration gets a strict delivery stanza: delivery.ci is the CI provider; delivery.argocd holds the project, the source (the address of the service's repository and the path of the base in it) and the environments (the location of the platform's environment files). The ApplicationSet takes the repository address from delivery.argocd.source. Every other field is refused with its path. It goes into ST-DECL-EN01 as the field Delivery stanza.

title: How does the ci-pipeline component state the pinned pipeline references and the trusted signers, and who gives their values?
description: Found by the Delivering builder, 2026-11-15, for finding N8b of the third walkthrough. ST-DLV-UC06-R01 and ST-DLV-INV04 say that the CI file takes each pinned reference and the trusted signer from the registry's ci-pipeline component, and ST-DLV-TD01 says that the fixture registry's ci-pipeline pins the shared pipeline and the STEGO checks by commit, the Konflux standard pipeline bundle and the STEGO checks bundle by digest, and names two trusted signers. But the registry holds no ci-pipeline component (ST-SUP-RC25 names registry/components/ci-pipeline, which does not exist), the component record ST-SUP-EN09 has no field for a pinned reference or a signer, and no record gives the real values: the repository and the commit of the platform's shared pipeline, the reference of the STEGO checks, the Konflux bundle digests, the keyless identity and the Tekton Chains public key. Options: (A) add a field Pipeline pins to ST-SUP-EN09, for the ci-pipeline component only: for each provider of ST-VO51, the pipeline reference, the STEGO checks reference and the one trusted signer, decoded strictly, each reference refused unless it is pinned (ST-DLV-SP02). The shipped component.yaml holds the values that the Product owner gives, and the fixture registry of ST-DLV-TD01 holds test values. (B) The same fields in one registry file of its own, such as registry/pipelines.yaml, out of the component. (C) The component ships with no provider until the Product owner gives the values; apply writes no CI file for a provider that the component does not cover (ST-SUP-RC25-OC01-T04), and the tests run on the fixture registry only. Recommendation: A, with C for the shipped values until they are given. The registry already versions each component, so one component change and a regeneration move every service to a patched pipeline (ST-DLV-INV04). The values are an owner-only step: only the Product owner can name the platform's shared pipeline and its signers. Until it is decided, and until ST-DLV-Q12 gives the provider field of the delivery stanza, ST-DLV-UC06 is stopped. Decided (A) with (C) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-15: ST-SUP-EN09 gets the field Pipeline pins, for the ci-pipeline component only: for each provider, the pipeline reference, the STEGO checks reference and the one trusted signer, decoded strictly, and a reference that is not pinned is refused. The shipped ci-pipeline component has no provider until the owner gives the real values; only the fixture registry of ST-DLV-TD01 holds test values.

title: Which pod security settings does the Kubernetes base write, and which cluster permissions may a component need?
description: Found by the security review of PR #351, 2026-11-15 (M1 and M2). M1: the base wrote the restricted pod settings only when a component stated the pod security level restricted, and never a read-only root file system, so a base could run with privilege escalation. M2: a cluster permission need could name secrets with list or watch, serviceaccounts/token, pods/exec, pods/attach, pods/portforward, pods/proxy, create on pods or an RBAC resource, with no resource names, and the base wrote a Role that could take over the namespace. Options: (A) the base always writes the restricted set (pod: runAsNonRoot and the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile; container: no privilege escalation, every capability dropped, a read-only root file system, with a bounded emptyDir at /tmp), which an overlay may relax and the base never does; and a cluster permission need on those sensitive resources is refused, a need may give resource_names, and get on secrets must give them. (B) The settings follow the pod security level of the needs, and a sensitive permission needs an acknowledgement in the declaration. Recommendation: A, which matches ST-SUP-RC15-OC01, OC02 and ST-SUP-RC16-OC01. Decided (A) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-15. The field Platform needs of ST-SUP-EN09 gets the optional shape field resource_names for a cluster permission.

title: How does the ApplicationSet reach the base, and which Argo CD project may a service name?
description: Found by the security review of PR #355, 2026-11-15. The ApplicationSet had two sources: the platform's overlay and a ref source on the service's repository. In Argo CD, a ref source works only for Helm value files, so it does nothing for a kustomize overlay, and the base was read from the default branch with no pin. Also, the project regex admitted default, which in a stock Argo CD allows every source and destination, and the service team chooses the environments repository and the project. Options: (A) the ApplicationSet has one source, the platform's overlay at the overlay path of the environment file, and the overlay pulls the base as a remote git resource pinned to a full commit, such as https://<host>/<org>/<service>//deploy/base?ref=<40 hex>; STEGO cannot write the overlay, so the plan, the docs and the file header state the exact resource line; the project default is refused, and the platform must give each service a locked AppProject (restricted sourceRepos and destinations, with kube-system and argocd refused); the revision of the environment files is the platform's choice. (B) The registry, not the declaration, names the environments repository. Decided (A) by the owner, 2026-11-15. The environment file has no field for the base ref, so stego env check has nothing to check there.

title: Which runs of the CI file may push and sign an image?
description: Found by the security review of PR #352, 2026-11-15 (M2). The CI file gave id-token, packages and attestations write to every push, on every branch and tag, and to each pull request from the same repository. The keyless identity of a shared reusable workflow is the same for each branch and each caller, so the trusted signer alone does not tell a main build from a branch build. Options: (A) the job that pushes and signs runs only on a push to the default branch and on a tag; a pull request gets a separate job with contents read permission only, which builds and tests but never pushes or signs; the Konflux PipelineRun names its event and its target branch; the signer of the registry may hold no expression ($ or braces). (B) Every run signs, and the verifier also checks the source repository and the source ref of the certificate. Decided (A) by the owner, 2026-11-15.

title: How does the Kubernetes base give the service its secrets and its configuration?
description: Found by the secret wiring research of 2026-11-15. The base wrote no env entry, so each platform team copied deploy/environment-variables.md into patches by hand, and a missing mapping was silent: the process stopped at start, or ran with a default. Options: (A) the base writes one env entry, names only, for each variable that the service reads: a secret variable takes valueFrom.secretKeyRef with the Secret <service>-<need> and its key; each other variable takes valueFrom.configMapKeyRef with the ConfigMap <service>-config and the variable name as the key; a required variable has no optional flag, and an optional one has optional: true; the defaults stay in the code, and the base never writes a value. STEGO also writes an opt-in kustomize Component, deploy/components/secret-files, that gives each secret as a mounted file (a read-only secret volume with the mode 0400, and the *_FILE variable) and removes the env entry, because the two forms are exclusive. (B) The base writes envFrom with one Secret and one ConfigMap. (C) The base wires nothing, as before. (D) The base gives each secret as a file only. Recommendation: A, so that the contract between the service and the platform is in the manifest, and a missing required key stops the pod with CreateContainerConfigError before the process starts. Decided by the owner, 2026-11-15: A (env references, and files as an opt-in), with the secret names fixed by STEGO. ST-DLV-Q19 gives how a variable names its secret need and its key.

title: How does an environment variable name the secret need and the key that give its value?
description: Found by the Delivering builder, 2026-11-15, during the build of ST-DLV-Q18. To write a secretKeyRef, the base must know the secret need and the key of each secret variable. To write the Component secret-files, it must know the secret of each path variable that names the file of a secret, such as STEGO_QUERY_CURSOR_KEY_FILE. No record states this link: postgres-adapter states the need {service}-database with the keys url, migration-url and worker-url, and the variables DATABASE_URL and the others, but nothing joins them. Options: (A) a variable states the optional fact secret_source, with the need name and the key, on a secret variable or on a path variable that names the file of a secret; the platform requirements keep it when the service states that need with that key, and drop it in other cases; the release test of the registry proves that each shipped source names a shipped need and key; a secret variable with no source, such as PGPASSWORD, gets no entry in the base. (B) A secret need states the variable of each of its keys. (C) The key of a secret need is the variable name, such as DATABASE_URL. Recommendation: A, because the variable list stays the one source of what the process reads, and a variable of one component can name the need of another (STEGO_RELAY_DATABASE_URL of postgres-adapter and {service}-database-relay of spicedb-authz). Built as A, with the field Secret source of ST-SUP-EN14 and ST-DLV-EN08, so that ST-DLV-Q18 can be built. Decided (A) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-15, because it carries out the owner's decision on ST-DLV-Q18. A source that the run does not keep makes stego validate, plan and apply warn with the variable, the need and the key. Security review of #370, H1 (2026-11-15): the serving Deployment got the credential of the owner role of the migration job. Decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-15 (least privilege): a variable that only the migration job reads states read_by_mode: migrate in the registry (field Read by mode of ST-SUP-EN14 and ST-DLV-EN08), and the base Deployment wires none of them; the Component projects only the keys that it switches, with items, so that no other key of a Secret is a file of the pod. ST-DLV-Q20 asks the owner about a migration Job of its own.

title: Does the Kubernetes base also write the migration Job, with a secret need of its own for the owner credential?
description: Found by the security review of #370, 2026-11-15 (H1). The base Deployment no longer wires the credential of the migration job (ST-DLV-Q19), but the key migration-url stays in the secret need {service}-database, which the Deployment reads for its other keys. So the owner credential is in a Secret that the serving pod references, and the platform must write the migration Job by hand. Options: (A) the base also writes a Job (or an Argo CD PreSync hook) that runs the binary with migrate, and postgres-adapter states a separate secret need {service}-database-owner with the key url for STEGO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL, which only the Job references; the Deployment never references that Secret. (B) Keep the key in {service}-database, and the platform writes the Job. (C) A separate secret need for the owner credential, and no Job in the base. Recommendation: A, because the owner credential is then in a Secret that no serving pod can name, and the migration order of a release is in the manifest. It changes the needs of postgres-adapter (ST-SUP-EN09), what the base writes (ST-DLV-UC07) and the environment files. Decided (A) by the Product owner, 2026-11-16: the schema migration runs as a Kubernetes Job of its own, which reads its own Secret <service>-database-owner; the serving Deployment, the Component secret-files and their projections never reference that Secret, and the key migration-url leaves <service>-database. An Argo CD PreSync hook is acceptable, but the Job must also work with plain kubectl apply -k and in local tests. The orchestrator decided the details under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-16: the Job is a plain batch/v1 Job of the base with the annotations argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync and argocd.argoproj.io/hook-delete-policy: BeforeHookCreation,HookSucceeded, which plain Kubernetes ignores; its name has a suffix from the digest of the release, because a new apply cannot change the pod template of a Job, and a name of more than 63 characters is refused with a clear message; it sets backoffLimit, activeDeadlineSeconds and ttlSecondsAfterFinished, and the restricted pod security of the Deployment with no fsGroup; it runs the service binary with migrate; and it takes the owner credential only from a secretKeyRef to <service>-database-owner, which the Component secret-files may change to a mounted file with only its key. On plain Kubernetes nothing runs the Job before the rollout, so the serving process checks at start that the migration ledger holds the last migration of its release, and else stops with an error that names the migration and tells that the migration Job must finish first (ST-SUP-RP14-LC07). LoadBase refuses a Deployment or a Component patch that references <service>-database-owner, and a Job that references another Secret. Built as ST-DLV-UC07-R06, ST-DLV-INV13 and ST-SUP-RP14-LC07.

title: Does STEGO keep a .containerignore and a .gitattributes rule in the author's project, and how?
description: Found by the security reviews of PRs #367 (I4) and #393 (L1), 2026-11-15 and 2026-11-17. With no .containerignore, the whole project folder is the build context of the Containerfile, so a local or remote builder gets files such as a local .env that the build does not use. With no .gitattributes rule, a checkout with core.autocrlf true writes CRLF into the Containerfile and the other files that STEGO owns, and the digest of the record then reports a hand edit. Both files are the author's files at the project root, where the author can have lines of their own; buildah and podman read only .containerignore or .dockerignore of the context root (no ignore file per Containerfile, which only BuildKit has), and the Containerfile is at the root, so a nested file cannot cover it. Options: (a) STEGO writes and owns each file whole; (b) STEGO keeps one marked block in each file and never changes a line outside it; (c) STEGO only documents the lines to add. Recommendation: (b). (a) overwrites or refuses the author's own lines, as the conflict prompts of Rails generators and the refusal of create-react-app in a folder with files show; (c) leaves the CRLF fault and the large context to each author. A marked block is the form that Ansible blockinfile, conda init and git lfs track use, and cargo init adds its lines to a .gitignore that exists. The .containerignore block comes first and ignores every path, then admits only what the Containerfile copies, so a later line of the author can admit more for a build of their own; the .gitattributes block comes last, so its eol rules win. Apply, not init, keeps the blocks, because apply writes the Containerfile and knows the files that STEGO owns. The record keeps the digest of each block, so apply refuses a hand edit inside a block, and it refuses a block whose markers are broken, naming the file and the line. Decision: (b), decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17.

title: How does stego env check know which variable carries the value of a topic need, and the value of an identity issuer need?
description: Findings B3 and U11 of the fifth walkthrough (2026-11-17). The platform requirements state the topic need inventory-events, and the environment file maps it to a real topic (topics.inventory-events.topic). But the Kafka destination sends to the value of STEGO_KAFKA_TOPIC, and no record ties that variable to the need. So an environment file whose STEGO_KAFKA_TOPIC names another topic passes env check, and the service sends to a topic that the platform did not make. The identity issuer need has the same gap: the declaration fixes the issuer (oidc-auth issuer), but the requirement holds no value, so an environment file that gives another issuer passes. PR fu/standing-3 already makes STEGO_KAFKA_TOPIC or its _FILE form a group of one of (kafka-topic), so a file that gives neither now fails; it does not compare the value. Options: (A) A need of kind topic or identity issuer MAY name the variable that carries its value (field variable, for example STEGO_KAFKA_TOPIC), and a need whose value the declaration fixes holds that value (the issuer URL). stego env check MUST refuse, as a value of the wrong type, a variable whose configuration value differs from the value that the environment file gives for its need, and an issuer entry that differs from the value of the requirement; a _FILE form is not compared, because the check reads no file. (B) The environment file gives the value once, in the need entry, and the delivery writes the variable from it (the overlay or the ConfigMap takes STEGO_KAFKA_TOPIC from topics.<need>.topic); the author never gives the variable by hand. (C) Keep the check of presence only, and say in docs/environment-file.md that the two must be equal. Prior art: Score (score.dev) lets a workload reference a resource output in an environment variable (${resources.bus.name}), and the platform fills it in, as (B) does. The Kubernetes Service Binding specification (servicebinding.io) projects each binding value into the pod by a fixed name, so the application reads one source. Cloud Foundry gives bound service values in VCAP_SERVICES, and Radius connections set environment variables from the connected resource; in each, the binding, not the author, writes the variable. Helm and Kustomize leave it to the author, as STEGO does now (C). Recommendation: A now, because it is a check only: it changes the requirement record (ST-DLV-EN02 gets the fields variable and value), the needs of kafka-producer and oidc-auth (ST-SUP-EN09) and the check (ST-DLV-UC02-R02), and no delivered manifest. Then B when the delivery writes overlays, which removes the second copy of the value. Not built. Decided (A) by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-17: a need names the variable that carries its value, or holds the value when the declaration fixes it (the issuer); env check refuses a mismatch as the wrong type. (B), delivery writing the variable from one source, follows when delivery writes overlays.

title: How does the Kubernetes base show a stopped worker mode without failing the API?
description: Found by the eighth walkthrough (W8-B4), 2026-11-17. The base writes one Deployment whose modes STEGO_MODE selects, all three by default, with the probes of health-check (ST-DLV-UC07-R03): /readyz stays 200 when the Kafka inbox stops, and only /readyz/modes of the service runtime answers 503 (ST-SUP-RP09-LC05). Kubernetes practice: liveness restarts a container and must not read a dependency, or an outage restarts every pod; readiness removes a pod from the endpoints of its Service, and a readiness that reads a dependency that every replica shares makes all replicas not ready at the same time, so a partial outage becomes a total one (the Kubernetes probe documentation; Colin Breck, Kubernetes Liveness and Readiness Probes, How to Avoid Shooting Yourself in the Foot; the AWS Builders' Library, Implementing health checks, on deep checks that take a fleet down). A pod that no Service selects takes no traffic, so its readiness only shows its state and holds a rollout. Web and worker processes run as separate process types in common practice (Heroku Procfile types, Rails with Sidekiq, Celery workers). Options: (a) the one Deployment takes /readyz/modes: a Kafka or audit sink outage stops the API, refused; (b) the one Deployment takes /readyz/modes only when the declared modes hold no api: right, but every walkthrough service holds api, so it shows nothing for them; (c) when the declared modes hold api and the worker or controller mode, the base writes two Deployments: <service>, with STEGO_MODE api, the probes of health-check and the Service, and <service>-worker, with STEGO_MODE worker,controller, liveness /livez, readiness /readyz/modes, no Service and no ingress port, each with the env entries of the variables that its modes read (read_by_mode), so the API pod holds no credential of the worker, relay or Kafka consumer; a service whose declared modes hold one side gets one Deployment with the readiness of that side. Recommendation: (c). It keeps the API ready through an outage of a dependency of the worker, shows a stopped worker in the Available condition, holds a release whose worker cannot start, and gives each pod the least credentials. Until then, docs/delivery.md gives the overlay that makes the split by hand. Decision: the recommendation, decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17.

title: Where does the authorization relay run when the api and the worker modes have their own Deployments?
description: Found by walkthrough 9 (W9-B2, W8-B6 again), 2026-11-18. Since ST-DLV-Q27 the base writes the Deployment <service> (api mode) and <service>-worker (worker and controller modes) (ST-DLV-UC07-R07). The relay of the destination authz runs in the worker mode only (ST-SUP-RP06-LC06), so with only the api pod up, the first administrator from Provision got 404 on create-shipment, and 201 after the worker pod started. Prior art: in the transactional outbox pattern the message relay is a process of its own beside the service (Richardson, microservices.io, Transactional outbox and Polling publisher; Debezium's outbox event router runs in Kafka Connect, not in the service); SpiceDB documents the dual-write problem and recommends a durable outbox or workflow over a direct write in the request (AuthZed, The dual-write problem). The outbox claims each message with a lease and FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so more than one relay is already safe (ST-SUP-RP01-LC03, LC05). Options: (a) document that the new rows and grants of the api pod are visible only after a worker pod runs, with the steps (deploy both, wait for the rollout of <service>-worker before Provision, one replica or more, monitor its Available condition); failure mode: an operator who runs only the api Deployment sees 404 and Authz-Revocation: pending until the worker runs, and loses no write; (b) the api Deployment also runs the relay of authz alone: the claim protocol already gives one delivery for each message, so no new lease is needed, but the api pod then holds the credentials of the worker and relay roles, which ST-DLV-Q27 removed (least privilege), its pool and its start depend on the relay, and a relay fault then reaches the API pod; (c) Provision also writes the tuples of the first administrators to SpiceDB in the request: a dual write, against the outbox-only rule (ST-DECL-UC06-R06, ST-SUP-RP06-LC09); a SpiceDB write before a rollback leaves a grant with no tenant, a write after the commit can fail and leave only the outbox copy, the write bypasses the revocation floor and its token, and it fixes only Provision, not the owner of a new row. Recommendation: (a). It keeps the least privilege of ST-DLV-Q27 and the outbox-only rule, and it loses no write: the failure is a delay that the revocation status shows. A later readiness hint, such as a warn event when a revocation stays pending past the wait cap, needs a runtime change and is not part of this decision. docs/delivery.md "The api Deployment needs the worker Deployment" gives (a). Decision: (a). The orchestrator decided this on 2026-11-18 under the Product owner's delegation: the api Deployment depends on the worker Deployment's relay, and the docs tell the operator to roll out the worker Deployment before Provision. Rejected (b), which gives the api pod the worker and relay credentials again (against ST-DLV-Q27), and (c), a dual write (orphan or lost grants, no revocation floor). Prior art: the transactional outbox and polling publisher; Debezium; AuthZed on dual writes.

title: How must a change that adds a key to SIGNERS and signs a fill with it be stopped from qualifying its own fill?
description: The security baseline of 2026-11-11 (finding 4) found that qualification reads SIGNERS from the tree it qualifies, so one change can add a key to a SIGNERS file and sign a fill with that key, and the fill is qualified in that change's own checks. ST-EXT-TM04 says that adding a signer is a reviewed change to SIGNERS, but no record makes that review separate from the sign-off it enables. Neither fix is allowed by the records as they are: ST-EXT-SP01 and ST-EXT-UC02-R02 say the project's SIGNERS file, which is the file in the tree, and the compiler runs in a project folder that need not have git or a base ref; and no UC requirement of ST-ASR-UC02 lets the change gate refuse a change for what it does to SIGNERS. Options: (a) qualification reads SIGNERS from a base ref that the caller gives, such as stego plan --signers-ref, and the tree's file only when no ref is given; this changes ST-EXT-SP01 and ST-EXT-UC02-R02 and adds a git dependency to every user project's compile; (b) a new UC requirement of ST-ASR-UC02: the change gate refuses a change that alters a SIGNERS file and adds or changes a fill sign-off in the same tree, naming both files; such a change is split in two, or merges by the owner's review and bypass, as a change to the CI definitions does (ST-ASR-UC02-R06); (c) no code change: CODEOWNERS requires the owner's review of every SIGNERS file, which holds only when the branch rule of the base branch requires code owner review (finding 1, the owner's). Recommendation: (b), with (c) as well: it keeps qualification the same for every user project, it makes the new signer a change of its own that the owner reviews, and the gate already reads both trees. The CODEOWNERS line for **/SIGNERS is in the workflows pull request of this hardening.

title: Which binding does a fill of the command, query or worker slot name, as it serves no collection?
description: Found by the fifth walkthrough (G2), 2026-11-17. The fills of commands, queries and workers ship in the binary with no test run, no evidence and no sign-off: stego test exits 0, stego fill status says that the declaration binds no fill, and plan and apply go on. The records already require the qualification of these fills: a command, a query and a worker each bind one fill of their slot (ST-DECL-INV39, ST-DECL-INV45, ST-DECL-INV68), their components emit these slots (ST-SUP-RC32-OC01, ST-SUP-RC33-OC01, ST-SUP-RC35-OC01), ST-EXT-INV05 names the contract package of the command and query slots, ST-SUP-RC35-OC03 wires a worker fill only when it is qualified, and plan and apply stop at a bound fill that is not qualified (ST-GEN-INV10, ST-EXT-UC02). So the missing tests, evidence and sign-off are a build gap. One design gap stays: ST-EXT-INV01 and the terms ST-EXT-TM01 and ST-EXT-TM07 say that each fill names and serves one collection, and a fill of a command, a query or a worker serves none. Options: (a) such a fill names no collection, and its binding is the one command, query or worker that names it; (b) its manifest puts the name of the command, query or worker in the collection field; (c) a new manifest field names the kind and the name of its binding. Recommendation: (a). The declaration already names the fill from the command, query or worker, so a second name in the manifest can only disagree with it; (b) gives one field two meanings, and (c) adds a field that holds a copy. Decision: (a), decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.

title: How does the baseline of a retype give back the column of the release before it?
description: The baseline migration 001_initial is the declaration with every schema step undone, and its body digest must be the one in the ledger of the release that runs. A retype keeps only From, the type before the change, so a retyped field that had constraints (max_length, min, max, values, a default or unique) cannot give back its old column, its checks and its indexes, and the baseline digest differs. Options: (a) a retype also takes the Definition of the old field, as a drop does (ST-DECL-EN21, ST-DECL-INV57), and the baseline reads the old column from it; (b) a retype takes From only and the old field must have had no constraint; (c) the baseline is read from the base record, not derived. Recommendation: (a). Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-13; it goes into the records and the code with the retype kind (ST-GEN-UC12, part 2b).

title: What does the release with a rename, retype or require at expand read for a row that the backfill has not reached?
description: ST-SUP-RC01-OC12 has the manifest of the release with an open rename, retype or require leave out the old column, so that release reads only the new column, which is NULL in each row that the backfill (ST-GEN-UC13) has not moved yet; for a required field that read fails or loses the value. Options: (a) the api replicas of that release stay not ready until the backfill of each open rename, retype and require is complete, while the release before serves, and the rollout has maxUnavailable 0; (b) the release reads coalesce(new, old) while the change is at expand, and needs the old column, so it cannot restart after the next release's contract (against ST-GEN-INV34); (c) the expand migration fills the new column, which holds one long transaction (rejected in ST-GEN-UC13). Recommendation: (a). Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: readiness reads the backfill status from the database (stego_schema.backfills), never from a flag that the replica sets itself; the rename, retype and require kinds wait for UC13 or for a real backfill status. It goes into the records with the rename kind. The owner replaced the readiness gate of (a) on 2026-11-13 (decision on finding F5 of the schema-change research, owner, 2026-11-13): the backfill runs in the migration job before the rollout, and readiness does not wait on it; a required field also needs failed_rows 0 or a covering fill value before the contract.

title: How does a release prove that a schema step trigger is its own, so the release before it accepts only a signed step?
description: ST-GEN-Q08 (e) adds a release-signed step record to the strict (c) rules: the expand migration of release N+1 writes a record of each step trigger, and release N accepts the step trigger only when the record verifies against a trust root built into release N and matches the catalog. Five points are open. 1. The trust root. Options: (a) the keyless sigstore identity of the release workflow of the service, the issuer and subject that the ci-pipeline component already names as the trusted signer of the images (ST-STD-TRUST-R04), with the sigstore trusted root (Fulcio and Rekor keys) built into each release; (b) a pinned Ed25519 public key built into each release, with its private key in a key store of the CI provider; (c) both, (a) for releases and (b) for local stand-ins. 2. What is signed. Proposal: one DSSE envelope of a JSON statement with the service name, the schema history step ID, the source and target release versions and the target image digest, the table with its schema, the columns K and U, the conversion, the template version, the SHA-256 of the function source as pg_proc.prosrc holds it with its SECURITY INVOKER and search path settings, and the trigger definition as pg_get_triggerdef gives it. Release N computes the digest and the definition from the catalog and accepts the step trigger only when they are equal to the signed ones; a replayed genuine record then admits only the genuine step. 3. Verification with no network at start. The record is signed in CI at build time, because its content is a build output, and the image carries it; the expand migration writes it to a table of stego_schema. With (a), the record carries the full sigstore bundle (certificate chain, Rekor inclusion proof and signed entry timestamp), and release N verifies it with the trusted root built into it, with no call to Fulcio or Rekor. With (b), release N verifies the Ed25519 signature only. 4. Rotation. Rule for both options: release N+1 is signed only by a root or a key that release N trusts. With (a), a change of the workflow identity or of the sigstore trusted root ships first in a release that trusts both the old and the new one, and only the release after it is signed by the new one. With (b), each release carries the current key and the next key, signs with the current key, and a rotation takes two releases. A record that no trusted root verifies is refused, and the start fails closed with a fault that names the step and the remedy (deploy the intermediate release). 5. Local and unsigned builds. Options: (a) fail closed: a build with no trust root accepts no step trigger, and the local suites use a local stand-in signer whose key the local build trusts, so the expand and contract path stays testable locally (AGENTS.md: a local stand-in for each hosted system); (b) a build with no trust root accepts a step trigger by the strict (c) rules and the interim rule (d) only, and logs a warning. In both options, a release-grade build without its trust root is refused by the release gate, so a production release never runs without it. Recommendation: 1 (c), with (a) for releases, because it reuses the signer identity that the images already have and adds no secret, and (b) only for the local stand-in; 2 as proposed; 3 as proposed; 4 the accept-both rule as stated; 5 (a), because (b) would make the strongest rule depend on how a build was made. Build after the strict (c) PR of the schema builder, which this extends. Decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: the recommendation, with three conditions. 1 (c): the keyless sigstore identity of the release workflow, with the sigstore trusted root built in, for releases, and a pinned Ed25519 key only for the local stand-in; a release-grade build never trusts the stand-in key: the release gate refuses a release-grade build whose built-in trust set holds a key that is not a release key, and a test proves it. 2 as proposed, and the envelope also binds the database and tenant scope it applies to (the service name and the schema), so a record cannot be replayed on the database of another service. 3 as proposed, and the table of stego_schema that holds the records is in the schema manifest. 4 as proposed, with the fault that names the step and the remedy. 5 (a), fail closed, with the local stand-in signer for the local suites (ST-STD-LOCAL); the private key of the stand-in signer is only in test fixtures, never a production key of the repository and never in a secret of CI. It is built after the strict (c) PR of the schema builder; the manifest reviewer and a second reviewer of the sigstore verification review it.

title: Must the committed record of what a service was built from hold the build identity of the stego binary that applied it?
description: Each PR that regenerates the examples writes, in examples/*/.stego/state.yaml, the build identity of the stego binary that applied it (revision, module_version and source_state of the compiler) and the registry_content_sha256. Two PRs that both regenerate always write different values on these lines, so the second one conflicts after the first merges, even when no component or generated file differs (#253, #261 and #262 on 2026-11-13). The orchestrator now resolves this at merge time with a regeneration from a clean clone (agents/followups/regenpr.sh), which costs a build and two applies per PR and one more CI run. The record is the one of ST-GEN-UC01-R05 (apply writes the record inside the service's repo). Options: (a) keep the build identity in the committed record, and keep the regeneration at merge time; (b) keep the build identity, but write it to a file beside the record that is not committed, such as .stego/build.yaml in .gitignore, so the committed record changes only when a component, a pin or a generated file changes; (c) keep it in the record, but let the examples' CI job compare the record with the build identity left out, and commit the examples with a fixed placeholder identity. Recommendation: (b), because a conflict on the committed record then means a real difference between two changes, and the build identity still exists on each machine that applied. (b) needs a change to ST-GEN-UC01-R05's contracts if they name these fields; (c) makes the committed record false on purpose.

title: Which direction does the sync trigger of a rename copy on INSERT and on UPDATE?
description: ST-SUP-RP15-LC02 rule 3 and its template version 1 (registry/runtime/manifest/sync.go, PR #270) say: on INSERT the function only sets NEW.U from NEW.K; on UPDATE it copies U into K only when U changed and K did not, and else copies K into U. ST-SUP-RC01-OC23 says: on INSERT it sets whichever of the two columns is NULL from the other; on UPDATE it copies from the column that changed into the other, and refuses the write only when both changed to values that differ after conversion. The two records do not agree, and only OC23 lets the rename release run. Under ST-SUP-RC01-OC12 the manifest of the rename release leaves out the old column K, so that the release runs on the schema of the next release after its contract step (ST-GEN-INV34); that release writes only U. With template 1, an INSERT of that release sets U := K, which is NULL: the new value is lost, and the INSERT fails on the NOT NULL of K, which the expand step keeps (ST-GEN-UC12-R02-T01). ST-GEN-UC12-R03 cannot be met. Options: (a) change rule 3 of LC02 to the direction of OC23, and replace the body of template version 1 with it (INSERT: IF NEW.U IS NULL THEN NEW.U := fwd(NEW.K); ELSIF NEW.K IS NULL THEN NEW.K := back(NEW.U); END IF; UPDATE: when only K changed, NEW.U := fwd(NEW.K); when only U changed, NEW.K := back(NEW.U); when both changed and NEW.U IS DISTINCT FROM fwd(NEW.K), RAISE with a fixed message that holds no row value; when neither changed, nothing). No release accepts version 1 yet: it is not on main and no runtime tag exists, so the body can change without a version 2. The release before a rename must then run a runtime that holds the new body, as for OC28 (ST-GEN-INV36). (b) keep LC02 and have the rename release write both K and U; then that release needs K and cannot run after the next release drops K at contract, against ST-GEN-INV34. (c) the expand step drops the NOT NULL of K and the rename release writes only U; the INSERT still loses U under template 1, so (c) does not work alone.
