Recommendation: (a), with a base check that refuses a rename, retype or require step when the base pins a runtime before that version, named in the fault as the release to deploy first. Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: rule 3 of ST-SUP-RP15-LC02 takes the direction of OC23, and the body of template version 1 changes in PR #270 before it merges, so that no runtime on main accepts the old body and version 1 has one meaning; the base check of the runtime version goes into the rename PR. Reopened by finding F3 of the schema-change research (2026-11-13): the NULL rule of (a) breaks a renamed or retyped field with a declared default, because the release of the step omits K, which takes its default before the BEFORE trigger runs, so a non-default INSERT is refused and an explicit NULL takes the default. Decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: the trigger takes its direction from a transaction-local writer marker, SET LOCAL stego.schema_step = '<change>', which the runtime of the release of the step sets; when the marker names the change it copies U into K, else K into U; a write that sets both columns to values that differ is still refused. This replaces the NULL rule of (a); rule 3 of ST-SUP-RP15-LC02 and ST-SUP-RC01-OC23 say so, and template version 1 changes in PR #270 before it merges.

title: May a rename keep the unique key of its field while both releases run?
description: ST-SUP-RP15-LC02 rule 2 has the schema check of the release before refuse a sync trigger whose old column K is in a unique key, so a rename of a unique field, such as User.email of ST-GEN-TD04, cannot run beside the release before; the rename kind refuses such a field at generation and names this question. ST-GEN-UC12-R02-T01, R03-T01, R04-T01, UC12-FL-T and the UC13 tests on ST-GEN-TD04 rename User.email and wait for it. Options: (a) accept K in exactly one single-field unique key of the manifest whose unique index the release before names, when the step gives U the same unique key by CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (ST-SUP-RC01-OC38), so both columns stay unique and equal; the release of the step needs a runtime that accepts it, which ST-GEN-INV36 enforces; (b) keep the rule, and change ST-GEN-TD04 to rename a field that is not unique, with a unique rename as a later kind; (c) keep the rule and refuse a rename of a unique field for good. Recommendation: (a), since a rename keeps the field's meaning and its key, and the check of the unique index stays exact. Written by the schema-change builder, 2026-11-13. Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: rule 2 of ST-SUP-RP15-LC02 accepts K in exactly one unique key, the single-field unique index of the manifest after the tenant column, when U has the same unique key in the exact step form, valid; the rename step builds that index by CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY and adds the sync trigger after it, in the migration <step migration>_sync (ST-SUP-RC01-OC22), so both columns stay unique while both releases run. Generation no longer refuses a rename of a unique field; a rename of a field in a unique key of more than one field, or of a reference, stays refused until its own design.

title: Where does a stalled backfill show now that it runs in the migration job?
description: ST-GEN-UC13-R06 and ST-SUP-RP09-LC12 make a stalled backfill fail the readiness of the controller replica and not its liveness. By the decision on finding F5 (owner, 2026-11-13) the backfill runs in the migration job before the rollout, and readiness does not wait on it, so no controller replica runs it. Options: (a) the job emits schema.backfill.stalled on the probe and keeps running until its backfill time limit, then fails with the stage migrate.backfill, and the next run of the job resumes from the checkpoint; no readiness changes; (b) as (a), and the job also ends at once on a stall; (c) keep a readiness signal by running the backfill in the controller as well. Recommendation: (a), which the built job does: Backfill.Stalled and the stall event stay in the lease runtime, and the job's time limit is service.BackfillTimeout (1 h by default). UC13-R06 and ST-SUP-RP09-LC12 keep their text until the decision. Written by the schema-change builder, 2026-11-13. Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: the migration job emits schema.backfill.stalled through the probe runtime and keeps going until its backfill time limit (1 h by default), then fails at the step backfill, and the next run of the job resumes from the checkpoint; no readiness changes. UC13-R06, ST-SUP-RP09-LC12 and the UC13 test records are restated from controller replicas to migration jobs.

title: Where does ST-GEN-UC12-R03-T01 prove a rename of a field with a declared default?
description: ST-GEN-UC12-R03-T01 has a second part on ST-GEN-TD04 "with a default on email": user C created through v2 with a non-default email, and user D created through v2 with no email "when the field is optional". In ST-GEN-TD04 User.email is required and unique, and a unique field with a default is refused (the check against the base refuses "both unique and a default"), so that variant of the data set cannot be declared, and an optional email is another declaration again. The first part (users A and B, each release reads what the other writes, both columns equal) runs on ST-GEN-TD04 as it is. Options: (a) restate the test to its first part on ST-GEN-TD04, and move the C and D part to a second rename in ST-GEN-TD04 v2 of a field that is optional and has a default (for example a new optional field Organization.description with a default, renamed in v2); (b) restate the test to its first part, and keep the C and D part at integration level, where ST-SUP-RP15-LC02-T01 (syncWrites: note has a declared default) and ST-SUP-RC01-OC23-T04 (writer marker) already prove it; (c) keep the test as recorded and change ST-GEN-TD04. Recommendation: (b), since the direction by the writer marker is a property of the trigger, which the integration tests prove on PostgreSQL with a declared default, and ST-GEN-TD04 stays one data set. Until the decision, ST-GEN-UC12-R03-T01 stays not automated yet; the first part runs inside ST-GEN-UC12-FL-T. Written by the schema-change builder, 2026-11-14.

title: Does ST-GEN-INV36 name the first runtime that accepts the sync trigger of the template version that the step gives?
description: Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: ST-GEN-INV36 names no template version. ST-GEN-INV36 refuses a new expand step of a rename, a retype or a require when the base pins a runtime library before the first version whose schema check accepts the sync trigger of template version 1. The decision on ST-SUP-Q120 (c) adds a completeness CHECK at expand, which every later write meets; under template version 1 a write of the release before to another column of a row that the backfill has not moved fails that CHECK, as version 1 sets the new column on UPDATE only when one of the two columns changed. So the step now gives template version 2, which also sets the new column where it is unset, and only runtime v0.95.0 and later accept version 2 and the CHECK: the pods of a base at v0.91.0 to v0.94.0 cannot restart after the step's migration. The built check (SyncRuntimeVersion) names v0.95.0. Options: (a) restate INV36 as the first runtime library version whose schema check accepts the sync trigger and the completeness CHECK that the step gives, with no template version in the statement; (b) keep the text and build the check at v0.91.0, which lets a base whose pods then cannot restart take the step. Recommendation: (a), which the built check does. Written by the schema-change builder, 2026-11-14.

title: How does the expand step of a require give each row there and each insert of the release before the fill value, when the field has no old column?
description: A require adds a required field with no default (ST-DECL-EN21 Kind), so the table has no old column K from which a sync trigger could copy, and the strict template form of the sync trigger (ST-SUP-RP15-LC02 rule 2) needs the pair K and U. Options: (a) the expand step adds U with the fill value as a constant DEFAULT, nullable, which PostgreSQL 11 and later store in the catalog with no rewrite of the table, so each row there and each insert of the release before, which leaves U out, reads the fill value at once; the CHECK of the field comes NOT VALID and a later migration validates it, as an add does; no sync trigger and no backfill; the contract step adds CHECK (U IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID, validates it, runs SET NOT NULL and drops the CHECK, and keeps the default, so that the release of the require beside the contract release still holds its manifest; (b) a new sync trigger form with one column that fills U when the writer marker is absent, and a backfill of the fill value: a new LC02 form and a new runtime version, with no gain over (a). Recommendation: (a). Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: no trigger and no backfill for a require; keep the default at contract, and a later step may drop it; restate ST-SUP-RC01-OC23, the notes of ST-GEN-UC13, ST-DECL-INV61 and ST-GEN-UC12-R01; a test proves that each row and each insert of the release before reads the fill value at once and that the table is not rewritten (its relfilenode stays).

title: Which column does the new type of a retyped field go into?
description: A retype keeps the field's API name and adds a new column U of the new type beside the old column K, so U needs a storage name other than K's, and no record named it. Options: (a) U is <field>_<new field type>, such as generation_string, cut over 63 bytes by the sha256 rule of the other generated names, and stays the field's column after the contract through the field's column, as a rename keeps its column; generation refuses a name that clashes with a column of the table; (b) the contract renames U to K's name, which a release of the retype beside the contract release cannot read. Recommendation: (a). Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14, as a technical choice.

title: How does a fill value that a later release adds to an open retype reach the sync function and the completeness CHECK of its expand step?
description: ST-GEN-UC13-R07 and ST-SUP-RP09-LC11 repair the rows that failed a retype with a fill value that the author declares in a later release (ST-GEN-INV33 admits only that change of an open retype). But the expand step of the retype wrote its sync function with the fill value as a constant, or NULL, and its completeness CHECK with OR (NOT <guard>) when it had no fill value, and the ledger digest covers that text: the migrations of a release with the new fill value differ from the ledger rows of the steps that ran, so its migration job refuses the ledger, and the sync function of the release before would still write NULL for a value that does not convert. Options: (a) the release with the new fill value gets one more migration of the change, step_<position>_<change>_fill_<n>, which replaces the sync function with CREATE OR REPLACE (the text of the template with the new fill value) and replaces the completeness CHECK NOT VALID in the same short transaction, and the migrations of the expand step keep their text as the baseline of the change; the release before must accept the new function text, so the schema check accepts a sync function of either fill value of the change (a new rule of ST-SUP-RP15-LC02, and a runtime that holds it first, ST-GEN-INV36); (b) the fill value is not in the function: the function reads it from the checkpoint row of the change (stego_schema.backfills.fill), so a new fill value is a row change that the backfill makes, and no migration text changes; this changes template version 2 into a version 3, which reads a table and so is not IMMUTABLE in spirit, and the release before must accept version 3 first; (c) a retype whose conversion can fail must declare its fill value at expand (no later repair), and ST-GEN-UC13-R07 becomes a repair by a new retype of the field. Recommendation: (c) now, as the smallest safe rule, with (a) as the later repair. The retype is built without the repair; ST-GEN-UC13-R07-T01 stays not automated until this is decided. Decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: (c). A partial conversion must declare its fill value at expand, and checking refuses it otherwise (ST-DECL-INV63); the check against the base refuses a fill value that a later release adds or changes (ST-GEN-INV33). The digest of the expand step stays fixed, no repair migration kind is needed, and the rule fails closed. ST-GEN-UC13-R07 and its test say that a later fill value is refused.

title: Where is the ST-BO09 question set kept, so a test can prove that the tour's self-check question is not in it?
description: Found by the builder of the architecture viewer (ST-GEN-UC08-R09), 2026-11-14: the guided tour must end with one self-check question that is not in the question set of the ST-BO09 study, but no record or file holds that set. The test ST-GEN-UC08-R09-T01 can compare the tour's question only with the study questions the design names, such as which fills can stop an operation. The viewer asks which steps of the walked flow run later, after the response. Options: (A) the platform team keeps the set in a file of the repository, such as docs/bo09-study-questions.md, and the test reads it; (B) the set stays outside the repository, and the tour's question stays a fixed text that the platform team checks by hand before each study. Recommendation: A, so the test proves R09 in full. Decided by the owner, 2026-11-15: no ST-BO09 study is planned soon, so the current check is accepted: ST-GEN-UC08-R09-T01 compares the tour's question with the study questions that the design names. Record the study set when a study is planned.

title: Does the same architecture model give the same export when only the input digests of its record change?
description: ST-GEN-UC17-R03 puts the input digests of the record in the header comment of each export, and ST-GEN-UC17-R04 says that the same architecture model gives byte-identical output. The model holds no digest (ST-GEN-UC08-R03-T02): a comment added to service.yaml changes the declaration digest of the record, and apply then writes the same model. So the header, and with it the export, changes while the model does not. Options: (a) R04 means the same model and the same record; the export is built so, and ST-GEN-UC17-R04-T01 proves the same model and record give the same bytes; R04 can say 'the same model and record'. (b) The header names only the record path and the hash of the model, and not the input digests, so the export follows the model alone; R03 then drops the input digests. (c) The header names the digests on a separate first line that a reader can leave out, and R04 holds for the rest of the output. Built as (a). Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-15: ST-GEN-UC17-R04 means byte-identical output for the same architecture model and the same record; the input digests in the header may change the export while the model stays the same. ST-GEN-UC17-R04-T01 proves the same model and record give the same bytes.

title: Do the second steps of the flows of ST-GEN-UC16 and ST-GEN-UC17 invoke their queries?
description: ST-GEN-UC16-FL-S02 (STEGO prints each fact with its source, marks each default, says which facts are unstated and claims no compliance) and ST-GEN-UC17-FL-S02 (the header comment names the record) invoke no query. So Lathe finds nothing that builds ST-GEN-UC16-R02, R03 and R04 and ST-GEN-UC17-R03, which those steps fulfill, and warns not-built, while ST-GEN-QRY06-H and ST-GEN-QRY05-H do the work and their tests prove it. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC16-FL-S02 invokes ST-GEN-QRY06 and ST-GEN-UC17-FL-S02 invokes ST-GEN-QRY05, as ST-GEN-UC14-FL-S02 invokes ST-GEN-QRY04; (b) S02 of each flow is joined to S01, which then fulfills all the requirements; (c) the warnings stay. Option (a) changes only two links of the design. Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-15: ST-GEN-UC16-FL-S02 invokes ST-GEN-QRY06 and ST-GEN-UC17-FL-S02 invokes ST-GEN-QRY05; the two links are changed with the Lathe CLI.

title: Is .stego/config.yaml an input of the service build record although it can hold a local registry path?
description: Found by the fourth walkthrough, 2026-11-15. The input manifest of .stego/state.yaml lists .stego/config.yaml with its digest, and the build record of stego build lists it as an input too, because it is a committed file of the revision. The file holds the registry sources, and on a workstation it can hold a local registry path. The records agree with this: ST-GEN-EN04 is each project file that apply read, and apply reads config.yaml to find the registry; ST-GEN-INV23 bars only absolute paths in the manifest, generated output and private state; ST-BLD-INV07 names every input of the revision. But a change of a local path changes the digest of the inputs when the registry content does not change, and ST-GEN-INV23 wants a moved project to keep its identity. Options: (A) Keep it: config.yaml decides the registry, so it is an input, and the registry content digest already shows when only the path changed. Document that a local path in config.yaml is a workstation setting, and that a committed config.yaml should name a Git source by commit. (B) Drop config.yaml from the input manifest and keep only the registry reference and the registry content digest of the record (a new manifest version). (C) Keep it, and refuse a committed config.yaml with a local path at stego validate. Recommendation: (A). It needs no format change, and the content digest already tells the two cases apart. No code changes until this is decided.

title: Does ST-GEN-INV14 cover the func init that protoc-gen-go emits in the protobuf code of an rpc-service?
description: ST-GEN-INV14 says that nothing in a generated service may register code by name, struct tag or init() to decide what runs. The rest-crud services now hold no func init: the postgres-adapter 6.7.1 registers the generated migrations through a call, and not in func init (ST-GEN-INV14-T proves this). The grpc-application component emits the Go code of the declared proto files with protoc-gen-go (internal_gengo). Each such file holds func init() { file_<name>_init() }, which registers the file descriptors and message types in the protobuf global registry. That registration does not select what runs: the generated main.go wires each service by a call. Options: (a) INV14 does not cover protobuf descriptor registration, because it decides nothing that runs; ST-GEN-INV14-T then also runs for rpc-service and exempts only files that start with the protoc-gen-go header. (b) INV14 covers it; the component then rewrites the emitted code so that the generated main.go calls each file's registration, which differs from the protobuf code that the rest of the ecosystem uses. Recommendation: (a). Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-17: ST-GEN-INV14 does not cover the protobuf descriptor registration that protoc-gen-go emits in func init, because it registers type descriptors and decides nothing that runs; every other generated init stays refused.

title: When does the version of the architecture schema change?
description: Found by the security review of PR #390 (info), 2026-11-16. The architecture schema kept the $id stego:architecture/1 when the access kind 'path limit' was added, so an older STEGO refuses a model that a newer one wrote, with a schema fault that does not tell why. Options: (a) change the version on each change of the schema; (b) keep the version on an additive change and let readers accept unknown values; (c) a semantic version of the schema, where a reader accepts a newer minor version. Recommendation: (a), with a clear refusal. The model feeds the compliance facts and the view (ST-GEN-RM04), so a reader that skips an unknown access kind shows less access than the service gives, a false negative; Swift (SE-0192, @unknown default), Rust (#[non_exhaustive]) and the open enums of proto3 exist because a new enum value breaks or silently changes old readers, and the Kubernetes API conventions call a new enum value a change that clients must be ready for. The model is derived output that apply writes again, so a reader needs no conversion: an older model asks for stego apply, and a newer model asks for the STEGO that the record names. (c) only helps when readers accept newer minor versions, which (b) shows is not safe here. Decision: (a), decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17.

title: Which component does a request flow of the architecture model start at, and what is the store step when no component is of the store layer?
description: ST-GEN-UC08-R05 says that a view is never guessed: a component that states no layer, flow part or port side is refused. But two parts of the request flows come from rules that no record states (follow-up of #341, limits a and c). (1) The handle step of every flow points at the first component, in the order of the active set, that is of the handler layer and has the setting expose. Today only rest-api matches. The command, query, worker, controller and domain-probe components are also of the handler layer, so a flow for a command, a query or a worker (ST-GEN-UC08-R12, walkthrough-5 U13) has no stated start, and a second component with expose would silently lose its flows. (2) When no active component is of the store layer, the store step points at the repository with the fixed text 'The store of <component> keeps the rows.', which is text that no registry part states (ST-GEN-UC08-R07). Options: (A) each component that serves operations states it in its architecture part, for example serves: [collection operations] on rest-api, [commands] on command, [queries] on query, [workers] on worker; a flow of a kind of operation starts at the one active component that states it, and applying a plan refuses to derive the view, naming the kind, when none or more than one does; the store step comes only from a component of the store layer or from a store that the repository's own architecture part states (store: PostgreSQL), and a repository with neither is refused as R05 refuses a missing layer. (B) Record the rules of today as they are, in a new requirement of ST-GEN-UC08, and refuse a second handler-layer component with expose; the fixed store text stays. (C) The archetype names the component that each kind of operation starts at, and the repository's store; a component outside the archetype cannot start a flow. Recommendation: (A). It follows R05 (the registry states each fact of the view), it is the form that architecture-as-code tools use (a Structurizr dynamic view and a Backstage component name each element that a step reaches, and infer none), and it gives the flows of commands, queries and workers of U13 a stated start. It changes component.yaml of rest-api, command, query, worker and postgres-adapter, and the architecture schema, so it should land with ST-GEN-Q43 (stego:architecture/2). Decision: (A), decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation (follow-ups list, 2026-11-15); a component states serves for the kinds of operation whose flows start at it, and the repository states store when no component of the store layer is active.

title: Through which repository and store does the request flow of a command, a query or a worker pass?
description: Found by the build of ST-GEN-UC08-R18 (fu-standing6, 2026-11-17). R18 asks for one request flow for each command, query and worker that passes the repository and the store. But the components command, query and worker require no port: none is bound to postgres-adapter or another component of the repository layer, so the registry states no repository for their flows. The runtime path reads and writes the tables of the service through the same database as the collections. Options: (a) the flow of a command, a query or a worker passes the repository and the store that the collection operations pass (the provider of the storage-adapter port of the component that serves the collection operations); (b) command, query and worker each require the port storage-adapter, so the binding names their repository as for rest-api, and a service with commands and no repository is refused as R05 refuses a missing statement; (c) the flow stops at the fill and states no repository, and R18 drops the repository and the store. Recommendation: (b). It follows R05 (the registry states each fact of the view) and Q44 (A); (a) is a rule that no record states, as the expose rule was; (c) hides the writes of commands and workers, which change events follow (ST-SUP-Q152). Check that a new required port changes no generated wiring (the assembler binds the port; the generators of command, query and worker read no adapter), else the component versions move (ST-SUP-UC01-R03). The rest of R18 (the operation step of the action, authentication for a command or a query, the decision of its permission, the serving component, a step of its fill, the outbox and each event and effect) needs no decision, but a fill step needs a new step kind in the architecture schema. Decision: (b), decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17: command, query and worker each require the port storage-adapter, so the binding names their repository as for rest-api, and a service with commands, queries or workers and no repository is refused, as R05 refuses a missing statement.

title: Is a missing generated file a hand edit?
description: Found by core7 in PR 408, 2026-11-17. stego apply (ST-GEN-CLI01) names every generated file that is missing or no longer matches its recorded hash, and writes nothing without --replace-hand-edits. So after the out folder is removed, or a fresh clone does not hold it, apply asks for --replace-hand-edits, and that flag also lets a real hand edit go. A missing file holds no work of a person to keep. Options: (a) a missing generated file is not a hand edit: apply writes it again with no flag, and the plan lists it as restored; stego drift still reports it as missing (ST-GEN-UC02); (b) keep the refusal, and add a flag --restore-missing that writes only missing files; (c) keep the refusal. Recommendation: (a). Generators with a record, such as Terraform (a resource deleted outside it is planned for creation, not refused), kubectl apply and Argo CD self-heal, recreate what is missing and keep the refusal for what changed. (b) adds a flag that authors learn to pass each time, which weakens the hand-edit guard as --replace-hand-edits does now. The record and the build still need the out folder in the commit (stego build reads out/commands, out/queries and out/workers from the revision), so (a) does not make an uncommitted out folder a supported workflow; it only removes a false refusal. Decision: (a), decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17: a missing generated file is not a hand edit; apply writes it again with no flag and lists it as restored, and drift still reports it.

title: How does a declaration remove an entity, and what keeps the old table and its authorization definition until the contract step?
description: ST-DECL-EN21 says that the Definition of a drop of an entity gives the removed entity's fields, and ST-DECL-INV58 says that the declaration no longer declares the entity. That is not sufficient. The baseline 001_initial, or the add step that made the table, must give back the table byte for byte (ST-GEN-INV33, ST-GEN-INV35): its tenant column and row-level security, its references and their foreign keys, its unique keys and upsert keys, and the search indexes that the collections over it give. The release of the expand step must also keep the definition of the entity in the authorization schema, because the release before still writes its relationships, and SpiceDB refuses a schema that removes a definition with relationships (ST-SUP-RC29-OC23). A list of fields gives none of this. Options: (a) the entity stays declared as it was, with its collections, and names the drop in a new attribute dropped_by; generation gives it no API, client, repository, handler or manifest entry from the expand step, keeps its table until the contract step, and keeps its authorization definition. This is the model-level way of Rails ignored_columns and of Django SeparateDatabaseAndState. (b) The Definition holds the YAML text of the entity and of each collection over it. (c) The baseline is read from the base record, which ST-GEN-Q07 rejected. For the authorization definition after the contract step: (1) it stays in the schema, with its relationships, while the entity stays declared, and a declaration version (ST-GEN-UC10) folds it; no runtime change; or (2) the migration job deletes the relationships of the resource type after the contract migration, then writes the schema without the definition; this needs a new step of the migration job (ST-SUP-RP14-LC03), a runtime change. Recommendation: (a) with (1). Option (2) can come later as its own change. Decision: (a) with (1). The orchestrator decided this on 2026-11-17 under the Product owner's delegation of that day, after prior-art review (Rails ignored_columns, Django SeparateDatabaseAndState, strong_migrations): the entity stays declared with dropped_by, and its authorization definition stays; option (2) can come later as its own change.

title: How does STEGO tell the author about an upsert key with no scope on a protected entity?
description: The delta security review of PR #212 (L2, low) found that an upsert key with no scope is tenant-wide: a peer in the same tenant can take a key first, and the 409 or the update branch tells that the key exists (the known limit of ST-SUP-RP10-LC25). The orchestrator asked for a generator warning for an upsert key with no scope on an entity that has a resource type. The compiler has no warning channel: a generator can only refuse (ContextValidator) or emit files, and stego generate and stego build print no advisories. Options: (a) add an advisory channel: an optional generator interface that gives advisory lines, which the compiler collects in preflight and the commands print to stderr, with the rest-api generator giving this one; this changes what the generate use case reports. (b) Refuse an upsert key with no scope on an entity with a resource type, unless the collection states that the key is tenant-wide on purpose (a new collection setting). (c) Keep the limit and state it in ST-SUP-RC20-OC13 and the rest-crud component README only. Recommendation: (a), since other review findings also ask for warnings, and a refusal breaks declarations that are correct today.

title: Which part writes the declared relationships of a row on create, update and delete: the command runtime, as for references, or the generated fill?
description: The developer walkthrough of 2026-11-13 (step 13) found that a created row's declared relationships are never written: ST-DECL-UC06-R04 and ST-SUP-RC29-OC05 say that a create, an update and a delete enqueue the declared tuples in the row's transaction, and spicedb-authz emits Write<Entity>Relationships for that, but no generated code calls it. The creator of a project with relationship owner (subject source caller) therefore cannot read, list or extend what it created. The generated CRUD code cannot call the mapper: it needs the authorization runtime's own handle, which the command handle does not expose (ST-SUP-RP06-LC10), and the command handle's Relate refuses in a command that declares no permission, such as a public create (ST-SUP-RP10-LC05); a fill also cannot decide on a row that has no relationship yet. The runtime already writes the relation of each reference when the row is written (ST-SUP-RP10-LC05). Options: (a) the runtime writes the declared relationships as it writes references: EntitySpec gets the entity's relationships (relation, subject type, and the subject from the caller, the handle's principal, or from a field); a create touches each tuple whose subject is set, an update that changes a field subject deletes the old tuple and touches the new one, and a delete deletes each tuple, all through the authorization handle in the row's transaction, joined to its revocation, with no decision beyond the command's (as for references); spicedb-authz then emits no Write<Entity>Relationships, and RP10-LC05 and RC29-OC05 state this; a runtime pin. (b) Relate in a fill may write a declared relationship on a row that the same handle created in this transaction, with no decision, also in a command with no permission; generated create, update and delete fills call it with <Entity>Tuples; a runtime pin, and a wider fill power. (c) Expose the authorization handle to generated code; this breaks ST-SUP-RP06-LC10 (no bypass). Recommendation: (a), because it gives one path for all tuples of a row, keeps the fill's powers as they are, and makes a caller subject the principal that the runtime already holds, so a client cannot choose it (ST-DECL-UC06-R04-T04). Decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: (a). The command runtime writes the declared relationships of a row as it writes the relations of its references, through the authorization handle in the row's transaction, joined to its revocation: a create touches each tuple whose subject is set, the caller's subject taken from the handle's principal; an update that changes a field subject deletes the old tuple and touches the new one; a delete deletes each field-sourced tuple from the row. spicedb-authz no longer emits Write<Entity>Relationships. Built on runtime v0.86.0. Delete path decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: option (1), a filtered delete, in the next PR on runtime v0.87.0: a delete of a row enqueues, in its transaction and joined to its revocation, the delete of every tuple of the row's resource and relation, for each caller-sourced relationship and each reference; the filter always names exactly one resource type, one resource ID and one relation, and the port and the adapter each refuse an empty one; a delete of one row leaves every tuple of another row intact. Leaving stale tuples (2) is refused: the lookup and list paths would still see deleted IDs, and a stale owner tuple would grant rights to an ID that a restore or an import brings back. Security review of PR #271, decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: (M1) a field-sourced relationship subject is set at create and cannot change after that; an update or a patch that changes it is refused with 400 that names the field, through a bad-request error of the runtime (ErrInvalid) that OutcomeOf maps to 400, so the runtime refusal is the guard for every interface and not the generated handlers only; a command that declares no permission may not write a field-sourced relationship, and the generator refuses that declaration; a declared transfer command for a field subject is a follow-up. (M2, L3) Every declared tuple is built and checked (the subject ID and its tenant) before the row statement; any failure after the row statement breaks the handle, so Run commits nothing; a hostile subject (*, a character that a provider ID cannot hold, the ID of another tenant) gives 400. Security review of PR #272, decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: (M3) a delete filter-deletes every relation that the entity's authorization definition declares on the row's resource, a list that the generator makes from the schema, so a tuple that a fill wrote is gone too; (L2) the relay refuses the filtered delete operation unless the payload has version 2.

title: Can the creator of a row read and list it right after the create, before the relay writes its tuples?
description: The developer walkthrough rerun of 2026-11-13 (main 2a8a5ff7, tasks v1) found that a GET of the tasks of a project right after two task creates listed 1 of 2. The relay writes the tuples of a create to the provider after the commit, so for a short time the creator cannot see the new row; a later list shows both. The spec allowed this gap and did not state it: each check is at least as fresh as the revocation floor (ST-SUP-RP06-LC09, ST-SUP-RC29-OC02, OC04), the relay raises the floor before a tuple is done (ST-SUP-RP06-LC13), and only a revocation has a status that its writer can read (ST-SUP-RP06-LC15, LC18). A consistency option alone does not close the gap, because at commit the tuple is not at the provider and no token exists yet. Options: (a) state the gap, and give the write a status that the client can read, as a revocation has; (b) a token that the relay records and that the client sends on its next list, so the list waits for that write or reads at least as fresh as it; (c) a list option for full consistency, which does not help before the relay ran; (d) the create waits for the relay, or writes the creator's tuples itself, which goes against the outbox-only rule (ST-DECL-UC06-R06, ST-SUP-RP06-LC09). Decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: (a) and (b). (a) Every tuple of a create already joins the transaction's revocation (ST-SUP-RP06-LC12, ST-SUP-RC29-OC05), so the write status is the revocation status: the command runtime answers Authz-Revocation: pending and Authz-Revocation-Location on each write that enqueued a tuple, and serves the status route, which honors Prefer: wait=N within the wait cap and the waiter limit (ST-SUP-RP10-LC35, ST-SUP-RP06-LC24, ST-SUP-RC29-OC16 to OC19). A create is visible to its creator once its revocation is complete. (b) The token that the client sends is the identity of its revocation, in the request header Authz-Revocation-After; the relay records the provider's token on that revocation when it lands. The list waits, within the same bounds and with no connection held, until the revocation is no longer pending, and then runs at the floor, which is at least as fresh as the recorded token (ST-SUP-RP06-LC13); it answers the state in Authz-Revocation (ST-SUP-RP11-LC21). The client never sends a provider token, so a client cannot give the provider a crafted or a stale token, and no two tokens are compared. The emitted list handlers call it in a later change of spicedb-authz and rest-api. Extended by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: a read GET /{id} honours Authz-Revocation-After the same as a list, so a single read right after the caller's write sees it (ST-SUP-RC20-OC42); and the OpenAPI document describes the request header Authz-Revocation-After, the response headers Authz-Revocation and Authz-Revocation-Location, and the status route (ST-SUP-RC20-OC43).

title: How does the backfill of a rename find the rows of a tenant that the tenant list does not hold?
description: Finding L1 of the security review of PR #291: lease.Copy walks only the tenants of stego_tenants, so the rows of a tenant that the list does not hold (a write with a tenant that was never provisioned, or a list row that was removed) are never copied, and the change is still marked complete; a later contract step then drops the old column and loses those values. The decision of 2026-11-14 says: take the tenant list from the table's own tenant column, read as the owner with a DISTINCT over the indexed tenant column by keyset, and refuse completion while any row has the new column NULL and the old column set. This cannot be built as written: each owned table has FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with the policy tenant_isolation (ST-SUP-RC27-OC03), and the owner role is NOBYPASSRLS, so the owner reads only the rows of the tenant in app.tenant. A SECURITY DEFINER function of the owner sees the same rows. A test on PostgreSQL 17.7 gave 0 distinct tenants to the owner for a table with rows of three tenants. Options: (a) in one short transaction at the end of the backfill, with the step lock timeout, ALTER TABLE ... NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY as the owner, read the distinct tenants of the table by keyset and count the unmoved rows, then roll back, so the table is never seen without FORCE; it takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the time of the reads; (b) add a policy FOR SELECT TO the owner role USING (true) on each owned table, which changes ST-SUP-RC27-OC03 and the schema check of the release before (ST-SUP-RP15-LC02); (c) give the step a NOT VALID CHECK (new IS NOT NULL OR old IS NULL) and VALIDATE it at the end of the backfill, which reads every row with no row-level security under a SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock; a failed VALIDATE refuses completion, but it does not find the tenants to copy, and the CHECK is a new object of the step manifest; (d) make the runtime refuse a write for a tenant that the list does not hold, so such rows cannot exist, and keep the walk over stego_tenants. Recommendation: (c) to refuse completion, with (a) for the tenant list, since (c) blocks no read or write and (a) holds its strong lock only for an index-only read. Until the decision, lease.Copy walks stego_tenants as before. Written by the schema-change builder, 2026-11-14. Decided (c) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: at expand the rename step adds a NOT VALID CHECK, one per conversion, named <table>_<new column>_complete: (new IS NOT NULL) OR (old IS NULL), relaxed by OR NOT <guard of old> where a conversion that can fail and no fill value give NULL; it comes in the migration of the sync trigger, before the trigger. The backfill marks the change complete only after VALIDATE CONSTRAINT passes in its own short transaction, which reads every row past row-level security and takes only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE (finding F2); a failed VALIDATE fails the job with a message that names the change and the CHECK, sets the checkpoint key back to the start, and the next run passes over the rows again. The schema check of the release before accepts the CHECK in its exact form, NOT VALID or validated, only beside the sync trigger of template version 2, which on UPDATE also sets the new column from the old one where the new one is unset, so that a write of the release before to another column of an unmoved row meets the CHECK; the manifest of the release of the step names the CHECK as an optional constraint that must be validated when present, and the contract step drops it. Option (a) is not used: it holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE (finding F1). Option (d) is not built: such rows can exist (a create of an entity with no parent is decided on the service resource and does not read the tenant list, no foreign key ties a row to stego_tenants, and an operator can delete a list row); a refusal in the tenancy layer is its own PR when the orchestrator asks for it. With it, backfill_checkpoint requires the lease name 'stego.backfill.' || the change ID (recheck of the security review of PR #291).

title: Does a database from a runtime earlier than v0.31.0 get an upgrade path from the shared outbox relay role to the per-service relay role?
description: Decided (b) by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: no handover; the outbox step refuses with a fault that names stego_outbox_relay and the remedy. Follow-up F4 (low). Since v0.31.0 the outbox relay functions belong to the per-service role <prefix>_outbox_relay. Before, they belonged to the shared role stego_outbox_relay. On a database from an earlier runtime, CREATE OR REPLACE of a relay function as the new role fails with 'must be owner', and the outbox step fails closed. The old role keeps its grants on stego_outbox.messages. No release of STEGO exists yet, so no such database exists outside tests. Options: (a) a guarded handover in the outbox migration: when a relay function belongs to stego_outbox_relay, ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO the new role, and then REVOKE the grants of the old role on messages, all in the outbox step's transaction; (b) no upgrade path, but the outbox step refuses with a fault that names stego_outbox_relay and the remedy (drop the old functions and the role as a superuser, and run the job again), instead of 'must be owner'; (c) keep the note 'no upgrade path' and change nothing. Recommendation: (b). No database exists from a runtime before v0.31.0, so (a) is code for a case that does not occur, in a step that runs as the owner role and changes ownership. That is the riskiest place to add code. (b) costs one catalog read and makes the fail-closed refusal readable. Build (a) only if a release before v0.31.0 is ever deployed. That cannot happen now, because the first release will use a later runtime.

title: Does stego_outbox.messages get an insert-time guard that refuses a sequence behind the highest sequence of its resource key?
description: Decided (c) by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: no trigger; the migration job check stays the guard, and the residual is recorded. Follow-up of the review and recheck of PR #256 (low, defense in depth). The claim order of each resource key follows the identity sequence of stego_outbox.messages. If the owner restarts that sequence below its rows, a later message can sort before an earlier one of the same key. The migration job already refuses a sequence behind its highest row (ST-SUP-RP14-LC03-T04), but only when it runs. The proposal is a BEFORE INSERT trigger, named in the schema manifest, that refuses NEW.sequence <= max(sequence) of the same tenant, destination and resource key, through the per-resource index. It needs a runtime version. Options: (a) the trigger as proposed. It has a race: two transactions that enqueue for one key take sequences 10 and 11, and when the one with 11 commits before the trigger of the one with 10 runs, the trigger refuses a correct write. Writers of one key are not always serialized, so (a) can fail real requests; (b) the trigger, and each enqueue first takes a transaction advisory lock on the hash of its key. That removes the race, but it serializes all writers of a key and adds a lock to every write; (c) no trigger. The migration job check stays the guard, and the residual is recorded: only the owner role can restart the sequence, and the same role can drop any trigger. Recommendation: (c). The guard defends only against the owner, who can remove the guard itself. (a) adds false refusals under load, and (b) adds a lock to the hot write path for a mistake that only the owner can make. If an owner-run check between job runs is wanted, the periodic maintenance job (audit_maintain runs as the owner) can compare the sequence with max(sequence) and alert. That costs no write-path lock and can be a later item.

title: Does the start check of the schema manifest also require the plain lookup indexes?
description: Decided (b) by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: plain lookup indexes are part of the start check, and a missing one alerts without failing closed. Follow-up #215 F2 (low), narrowed by #218. ST-SUP-RC01-OC12 says that startup fails closed when the database's schema, triggers or indexes do not satisfy the schema manifest. Since #218, the runtime check (manifest.Check) holds the tables, columns, types, defaults, constraints, policies, grants, triggers and functions, each unique index, and each index with an expression or a predicate. It does not hold a plain lookup index (columns only, no predicate), such as the index of a field that a list searches. If such an index is dropped, nothing reports it: reads stay correct, but a list scans the whole table. Options: (a) the manifest names each plain lookup index, and Check fails closed when one is missing or has other columns; (b) Check requires each plain lookup index, but a missing one gives the start warning and alert of F10, and the service starts; (c) no change, with the scope of OC12 restated as the indexes that correctness or isolation needs. Recommendation: (b). A missing lookup index is a performance and availability fault, not a correctness or isolation one. Failing closed would stop every replica when an operator drops an index for maintenance, so the cure would be worse than the fault. A start alert makes the drop seen within one rollout, at the cost of a catalog read at start. OC12 then says that a missing lookup index alerts and does not fail closed. The extra-index rule stays as it is.

title: How does the service keep every row of an owned table tied to a tenant that the tenant list holds?
description: Follow-up of PR #300 (Q120 (d)). Rows can exist for a tenant that stego_tenants does not hold: a create of an entity with no parent reads no tenant list, no foreign key ties a row to the list, and an operator can delete a list row while the tenant still has rows. Q120 (c) already guards the completion of a backfill: the validated completeness CHECK reads past row-level security, so the change stays open while such a row has the old column set. But the tenant iterator (ST-SUP-RP04-LC07) and every other per-tenant pass still skip those rows. Options: (a) a foreign key from the tenant column of each owned table to stego_tenants (tenant_id), added NOT VALID and validated by the migration job, so a write of an unlisted tenant fails and a list row with rows cannot be deleted; (b) a trigger on stego_tenants that refuses the delete of a list row while an owned table has rows of that tenant, and a check at create that the tenant is listed; (c) no change: the list is advisory, and each pass that must see every row reads past row-level security as Q120 (c) does. Recommendation: (a). It is enforced by the database for every writer, it costs one index probe of the primary key of stego_tenants for each insert, the tenant column of each owned table already leads an index, so the delete check is an index probe too, and NOT VALID with a later VALIDATE takes no lock that blocks writes. A tenant must then be provisioned before its first write, which provisioning already does (ST-SUP-RP04-LC07). Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14, with these conditions: ON DELETE NO ACTION (or RESTRICT), never CASCADE or SET NULL; the foreign key named in the schema manifest of each owned table; ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID in a text after the tenant list, under the lock timeout and the retry of a migration text; VALIDATE in the migration job, which refuses with a remedy (provision the tenant or remove its rows) when a row of an unlisted tenant fails it, as for Q120 (c); a proof that each owned table has an index that leads with the tenant column; and a test that the WITH CHECK of row-level security still refuses a write of another tenant, listed or not. The build waited until tenant provisioning (ST-SUP-RC27-OC09 to ST-SUP-RC27-OC13) was built (PR #315). The foreign key is now built, on runtime v0.104.0 (orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14): the schema manifest of each owned table names its tenant key <table>_<tenant column>_fkey (manifest.Table.TenantKey, ST-SUP-RC01-OC40), with an index that leads with the tenant column; the migration job adds it NOT VALID after the tenant list (step tenant_keys) and validates it (step tenant_keys_validate, ST-SUP-RP14-LC03). PostgreSQL 17 validates a foreign key with one query as the owner role, which under FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY sees only the rows of one tenant and so passes a table with rows of unlisted tenants; the validation therefore revokes SELECT on the table from the owner role in its own transaction, so PostgreSQL checks each row past row-level security, and grants it again. A release before the key does not accept it in its schema check, so a rollback goes only to a release that has the key.

title: On which resource are Provision and Retire decided: service:<service name> or the form of the caller's tenant?
description: Decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: Provision and Retire are decided on the unqualified, platform-only resource <resource type>:<service name>, such as service:todo-svc, as ST-SUP-RC27-OC09 states, and not on service:<caller tenant>/<service name>; it is the second exception of ST-SUP-RP06-LC22, beside the floor marker. Finding M1 of the security review of PR #315: the runtime decided on the tenant-qualified form of the caller's tenant, so a tenant administrator who holds operator on the service resource of their own tenant (service:<org-a>/orders), which a fill of that tenant can grant, provisioned and retired any other tenant (reproduced against SpiceDB v1.57.0). Options: (a) the unqualified resource of the whole service, which only the platform operator can grant; (b) the tenant-qualified form of a fixed operator tenant, which needs a tenant that is not a customer and a setting for it; (c) keep the form of the caller's tenant and refuse any caller tenant but one, which ties Provision to one tenant ID. Decision: (a). It is what OC09 states. No tenant-bound handle, relay path, fill or generated code can write a tuple on the unqualified ID, because the handle and the relay refuse every tuple that is not tenant-qualified (keyIn), so only an operator who writes to SpiceDB directly grants it. The proof: ST-SUP-RP06-LC22-T08 (the handle, Port and the relay refuse the ID, and a per-tenant grant decides nothing) and ST-SUP-RC27-OC09-T03 (a grant of operator on service:<org-a>/wiring-shop provisions and retires no tenant, against a real SpiceDB).

title: What does the contract step do about a release that cannot report itself?
description: Under the decision on finding F8 (owner, 2026-11-13) each process reports its release in stego_schema.releases (ST-SUP-RP09-LC14), and the contract step refuses while a release that does not know the change reports (ST-SUP-RC01-OC44). Two cases stay open. First, a release on a runtime library before v0.103.0 writes no report, so the contract step cannot see it and goes on. Second, an expand step that a postgres-adapter before 6.4.0 generated made no table of the reports, so the contract step of that change refuses until a person makes the table. Options: (a) state both as limits in docs/schema-changes.md, beside the rule that a release which is not deployed before the next one is the operator's risk (ST-GEN-UC14-R05), and keep the refusal on a missing table; (b) add a base-check refusal, as ST-GEN-INV36 does, of a contract step whose base pins a runtime library before v0.103.0 or a postgres-adapter before 6.4.0 at the expand of the change; (c) also read pg_stat_activity and refuse while a session of the runtime role has no release label in application_name. Recommendation: (a) now, as no service on main has an open change from before these versions, and (b) as a follow-up under finding F11. Written by the schema-change builder, 2026-11-14.

title: Is the service-level resource of a top-level create tenant-qualified?
description: Finding G3 of the walkthrough re-run (2026-11-14). ST-SUP-RC29-OC01 and ST-SUP-RP10-LC31 say that the create of an entity with no parent is decided on the service-level resource <resource type>:<service name>, such as service:todo-svc, as Provision does, and ST-SUP-RC27-OC09 says that this resource is not tenant-qualified. But ST-SUP-RP06-LC22 says that only the tenant decision of the handle evaluates the unqualified resource, and the notes of ST-SUP-RP10-LC31-T03 say that the resource ID of the create is tenant-qualified, as every resource ID is. The runtime follows LC22: Run decides the create on service:<base64url tenant>/<base64url service name>. So the operator grant service:tasks#operator, which allows Provision, does not allow create: provision; a grant on the tenant-qualified ID does. Options: (A) keep the tenant-qualified ID for a create, and change OC01 and LC31 to say so: a grant then allows a create in one tenant only, and the operator or a declared relationship writes it per tenant; (B) decide the create on the unqualified ID, as Provision: one operator grant allows a create in every tenant whose token the caller holds, and LC22 gets a third exception. Recommendation: A, because a grant in one tenant then never allows an act in another (the rule of LC22), and the runtime and its test already do it; the generator (fu-72) is the same for both options. Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: keep the tenant-qualified create resource, and correct the wording of ST-SUP-RC29-OC01 and ST-SUP-RP10-LC31 (provisioning alone uses the unqualified service:<svc>). Recorded with the low finding of the security review of PR #317: checking refuses a top-level create whose permission is the provision or retire permission.

title: How do the views carry NULL for an optional field when fills read the same value type?
description: Finding of the walkthrough re-run (2026-11-14): a PUT that leaves out an optional string field stores NULL, but each read answers "" for it. The read-only value of an entity (capability.ValueOf, goTypeOf) reads a NULL column as the zero value of its Go type, so no field is a pointer; the rest-api handlers build their answer from the view that the query component gives them (query.ViewFile, the type <Entity>View, ST-SUP-RC33-OC09) and give each optional field as ptrOf(v.<Field>), which is never nil. So a client cannot tell an unset optional field from "", 0 or false, and a create that sends "" answers the same as one that sends nothing. An optional jsonb field is already nil for NULL, and an optional timestamp answers no value for NULL since #321. The orchestrator decided under the owner's delegation (2026-11-14) that the query views carry NULL for optional text; the same value type is what a fill reads through the query handle (ST-SUP-RP11-LC12) and the command handle (ST-SUP-RP10-LC15), so the change can reach the fill read contract. Options: (A) give every optional field as a pointer in the read-only value, nil for NULL, in the views and in the loaded values that fills read: one rule everywhere, but each fill that reads an optional field must change, which needs a major version of the archetypes and a fill change in each such service; (B) give the pointer form only in the <Entity>View type that query.ViewFile makes for the rest-api handlers, which no fill reads, so answers leave out a NULL optional field, as the API schema allows, and the loaded values of fills do not change; (C) no change: document that an unset optional field answers its zero value. Recommendation: B. It fixes the answer with no fill change, and A stays open for a later major version if a fill needs to tell unset from empty. Decided (B) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: each optional field that is not a slice is a pointer, nil for NULL, only in the <Entity>View type that query.ViewFile makes for the rest-api handlers; the loaded values that fills read do not change. Built in PR #328 (ST-SUP-RC20-OC37-T12), with the read check of an optional implicit field, which treats NULL as not found (ST-SUP-RC20-OC23-T07).

title: What does the parent chain check of a scoped collection decide on each ancestor of the path?
description: Decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: A. Reason: a check at each level with the read permission, and one 404 for a missing, denied, wrong or foreign ancestor, does not show which ancestors exist (OWASP: no existence leak, and least privilege). A list under a refused parent now gives 404, not 200 with no items. Finding N2 of the walkthrough re-run (2026-11-14): a collection scoped under a scoped collection, such as tasks under projects under orgs, was refused. The rest-crud spec document (Multi-level scope, Path Derivation Rules 3) derives the path of every ancestor and asks for parent existence verification at each level; ST-SUP-RC20-OC24 says only that a read, update, patch or delete checks that the stored record belongs to the parent named in the path. No record says what the check decides on an ancestor above the parent, or on the parent of a list, a create or an upsert. b-scope/nested builds this rule: every handler of a scoped collection, each operation and each level, the parent included, reads each ancestor that the path names in the tenant through the command or the query handle, which decides the read permission that the entity of the ancestor declares, and requires that the scope field of each ancestor names the ancestor above it in the path; a missing, denied or wrong ancestor is 404, the same answer for each, and a list under such a parent is 404 (before, a list under a missing parent of one level answered 200 with no items). A create still decides the permission of its reference on the parent (ST-SUP-RP10-LC05). Each level adds one read and one decision to each request. The chain follows the first declared collection of each ancestor entity, as the path does. Options: (A) the rule as built; (B) existence and the link of each ancestor only, with no decision on an ancestor: the permission of the row itself is the only decision, and an ancestor that the caller may not read still answers the rows below it; (C) a decision only on the ancestors above the parent, so a collection of one level keeps its answers. Recommendation: A, because a caller who may not read an ancestor learns nothing of the rows below it, every level answers the same, and the path names nothing that is not checked. If A is accepted, ST-SUP-RC20-OC24 needs the statement: every handler of a scoped collection MUST read each ancestor that the request path names in the tenant, with the read permission of its entity, and MUST check that it is of the ancestor above it, and answer 404 for a missing, denied or wrong ancestor, before it reads or writes a row.

title: Which values may a component give for its part in a request flow and for the side of each port?
description: Finding N8 of the walkthrough re-run (2026-11-14): apply writes no architecture view (ST-GEN-UC08), and the view places each component from its architecture role alone (ST-SUP-EN09, field 8; ST-SUP-UC01-R05). The field lists the layers (edge, authentication, handler, slot, repository, store, outbound) but gives no values for the part in a request flow or for the side of a port; its example is free text. ST-GEN-UC08-R04-T02 needs the view to order the steps of a flow (the operation, authentication, the handler, each slot, the repository, the store, each event), which free text cannot order. Options: (A) the flow part is one short sentence that the view shows, the order of a flow comes from the layer order, and the side of each port is one of inbound (the flow comes into the component through the port) or outbound (the component calls on through the port); (B) the flow part is one of a closed list of steps, such as receive, authenticate, handle, fill, persist, store, publish, and the side as in A. Recommendation: A. The layer list already gives the order of R04-T02, and a sentence keeps the view readable without a second list to keep. Until it is decided, ST-SUP-UC01-R05 and ST-GEN-UC08 are not built; ST-GEN-UC08 also waits for ST-DLV-Q04, for its platform edges. Deferred by the orchestrator, 2026-11-14: the architecture view design is under owner review, so ST-SUP-UC01-R05 and ST-GEN-UC08 stay not built and this question stays open. Decided (A) by the owner, 2026-11-14, with the slot phase, as section 3.4 of the architecture view proposal gives: the flow part is one plain sentence of at most 100 characters, which the view shows; the side of each port is inbound or outbound; the order of a flow comes from the layer order, and each slot states its phase, before store or after store (ST-SUP-EN08). A flow then runs: edge, authentication, handler, the slots of phase before store in the order the offering component lists them, repository, store, the slots of phase after store in the same order, then the outside calls; each event that the store writes to the outbox is a sync outbox step, and then an async event step. The layer outbound is renamed outside call, so that it does not clash with the port side outbound. ST-SUP-EN09 field 8, ST-SUP-EN08, ST-SUP-UC01-R05, ST-SUP-SP05, ST-GEN-DS04 and ST-GEN-UC08 state the decision.

title: Which declared setting selects the worker component, which is alpha?
description: ST-SUP-RC35 is alpha, so ST-SUP-SP01 keeps it out of every archetype and mixin, and ST-GEN-INV37 names the settings that select a component (tenancy, audit, authorization, idempotency, a ledger) but not workers. So no declaration could get the worker component, and no generated service had a worker. Options: (a) a declared worker selects worker, with the experimental acceptance that INV37 asks while it is not ga; (b) make RC35 ga and add it to the archetypes; (c) a mixin async-worker that the archetypes list as compatible, which SP01 refuses while RC35 is alpha. Recommendation: (a), which the build of RC35 (PR of b-worker/rc35) carries out now as the reading of INV37 that a declared setting selects the component it implies; add workers selects worker (ST-SUP-RC35) to the list of ST-GEN-INV37. Decision: (a). A declared worker selects the worker component, with the experimental acceptance that INV37 asks while RC35 is not ga, as internal/compiler/selection.go reads it. Decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14. The Product owner writes the setting workers into the list of ST-GEN-INV37.

title: How is the tuple of a worker in a tenant written, and how does it reach the permission of a resource?
description: ST-SUP-RC35-OC13 asks for the tuple tenant:<tenant id>#worker_<name>@service_account:<name> at each provisioning. Two parts are open. First, the authorization handle and the relay refuse each tuple whose resource ID is not tenant-qualified (ST-SUP-RP06-LC22), and the tenant ID of the tuple is not, so the relay would refuse it; the options are a tenant resource whose ID is the tenant-qualified form of the tenant with an empty key, which the relay accepts as is, or a second exception to LC22 beside the service-level resource. Second, no record makes the runtime write a relation from a resource to its tenant, such as order#tenant@tenant:<id>, so a permission such as sync = tenant->worker_sync_partner_orders can never be allowed, and the tuples would grant nothing. Recommendation: the tenant resource takes the tenant-qualified ID (no new exception to LC22), and the runtime writes <type>#tenant@tenant:<qualified id> on each create in the revocation of the transaction, as it writes owner, for each type whose schema has the relation tenant: tenant. Until it is decided, OC13 (but its schema check) and ST-DECL-UC10-R03 stay unbuilt. Decision: the recommendation. The tuple of a worker names the tenant resource with the tenant-qualified ID, and the runtime writes <type>#tenant@tenant:<qualified id> on each create. Decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14. A later PR builds it; this PR keeps the schema check of OC13, and the tuples of OC13 and ST-DECL-UC10-R03 stay unbuilt until that PR.

title: What is the span of a worker run, which the telemetry runtime cannot name as OC09 says?
description: ST-SUP-RC35-OC09 asks for one span named worker <worker name> with stego.outcome committed, rolled_back, fenced or panicked. The telemetry runtime takes only span names that SpanNames registers at start, of lower-case letters, digits, dots and underscores (no space and no declared name), and its outcomes do not hold fenced or panicked; RunWorker already reports each run as the span command.worker with committed or rolled_back. Options: (a) keep the span command.worker and add the attribute stego.worker with the worker name and the outcomes fenced and panicked to the telemetry runtime; (b) register one span name worker.<name in snake case> for each declared worker at start. Recommendation: (a), so the span names stay fixed; the built-in event worker.run.failed carries the fixed outcome now (ST-SUP-RC35-OC09-T02). Decision: (a). The span stays command.worker, the attribute stego.worker carries the worker name, and fenced and panicked are values of stego.outcome; the build of RC35 carries it out (ST-SUP-RC35-OC09-T01). Decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14. The Product owner writes the span command.worker and the attribute stego.worker into the statement of ST-SUP-RC35-OC09.

title: Which collection operations call each slot?
description: Found by the builder of the architecture model (ST-GEN-DS04, ST-GEN-UC08-R04), 2026-11-14: a slot states its name, its component, its contract and its phase (ST-SUP-EN08), but not which operations of a collection call it. The declaration binds a slot to a collection, not to an operation. Only the code of the rest-api generator holds it today: validate runs for create, update and upsert, on_entity_changed for each write, and before_<operation> and after_<operation> for their operation. The request flows of the architecture model cannot place a slot from the registry alone (ST-GEN-INV11), and a name rule is a guess, because validate and on_entity_changed follow none. Options: (A) the slot states its operations, the collection operations that call it, as a new field Operations of ST-SUP-EN08, which the registry decoder requires beside the phase, and the flow places each slot from it alone; (B) the flow takes the operation from the slot name before_<operation> or after_<operation>, and a slot with another name must state its operations. Recommendation: A, one rule for every slot and no reading of names. Decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: (A).

title: Which role may a consuming worker write as, when its run is a transaction of the outbox worker?
description: RunConsumer runs the fill of a worker with a consumes trigger in the transaction of the outbox worker that claimed the message, so the message is done only when the fill's writes commit (ST-SUP-RC35-OC06). That transaction is a session of the worker role. The role migration (ST-SUP-RC27-OC04) and the migration job (ST-SUP-RP14-LC03) give the worker role only the outbox functions, the enqueue columns of the queue and the default audit sink; the grants of the entity tables and of idempotency_keys go to the runtime role only. So each consumer run fails on its first statement: in the generated service of testdata/runtime_wiring, the key row of the idempotency wrapper fails with permission denied for table idempotency_keys (SQLSTATE 42501), and the message stays pending and is held back. The schema manifest (ST-SUP-RP15-LC01) holds exactly the grants of each table, so a grant by hand is not a way out. Options: (a) when the declaration has a consuming worker, the migration job also gives the worker role the grants of the runtime role on the tables of the entities that a consumer writes, on idempotency_keys, and on the audit and authorization tables that a run writes, and the manifests hold them; (b) the role migration makes the worker role a member of the runtime role with INHERIT TRUE, as the tests of the command runtime do; (c) RunConsumer runs the fill in a transaction of the runtime role's pool and marks the message done in the transaction of the outbox worker after that commit, which gives up the one commit of OC06. Recommendation: (a), the least grant. Decision: the worker role gets on idempotency_keys the privileges that a consumer needs, SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE only, under the same row-level security and tenant policy as the runtime role, and nothing more; the migration job grants them when the declaration has a consuming worker. Decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-15. The Product owner writes the grant into ST-SUP-RC27-OC04 and ST-SUP-RP14-LC03.

title: Must a release wait until SpiceDB serves its schema, and must a decision that the provider cannot make now answer 503 with Retry-After, and every other provider failure 500?
description: The third developer walkthrough (2026-11-15, G4) found that for about 5 s after a release adds a resource type, each list of it answers 500 internal error, and no log names a cause. SpiceDB reads a check at least as fresh as an older floor at a quantized revision, which for some seconds after a schema write does not know the new definition: it answers ERROR_REASON_UNKNOWN_DEFINITION. The query runtime made that an undecided read, and the generated handler answered every error that was not 404 or 400 with 500. No record says that the migration job waits for the schema, or how a handler answers an undecided read or command. ST-SUP-RP14-LC03 lists the steps of the job and has no wait; ST-SUP-RC20-OC03 lists the error categories and has none for 503. Built: (a) the job reads the schema token before its first schema write and, after the last write, a step authorization_schema_served waits until SpiceDB serves each definition of the written schema to a read at least as fresh as that token, two probe rounds in a row, at most 120 rounds 250 ms apart, each probe within its own deadline of 2 s, and else fails closed with authz.ErrSchemaNotServed, so the release does not start; (b) for reads and commands alike, a decision that the provider cannot make now, a transient cause (a definition not served yet, a provider that does not answer or has no capacity, a call that ran out of time; authz.Transient), answers 503 with Retry-After of 1 to 3 whole seconds at random and the code <PREFIX>-INT-001, and every other provider failure (a refusal, a bad key, a conditional permission, an invalid resource) answers 500; the query and command runtimes log a warning with the entity or step and a fixed cause name (authz.Cause), at most one line for each cause in each 10 s with the count held back, with no provider text, subject or row key. Options: (1) accept (a) and (b) as built, add the step to ST-SUP-RP14-LC03, and state the answers and the INT category of 503 in ST-SUP-RC20-OC03 and ST-SUP-RP11-LC06; (2) accept (b) only and rely on the 503 during the window; (3) another bound or Retry-After value. Recommendation: (1). Written by the walkthrough-3 fix builder, 2026-11-15; restated after the security review of PR #354 (L2, L3, I2). Decided (1) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-15: the built behaviour is accepted; the design records are to state it.

title: Which grants does a consuming worker get, and what does a missing grant, a retired tenant or a failed tenant list do to a worker run?
description: The security review of PR #337 (worker component ST-SUP-RC35) found these faults. M1: RunConsumer runs the fill of a consuming worker in the transaction of the outbox worker, a session of the worker role. The decision on ST-SUP-Q136 gives the worker role only SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE on idempotency_keys. So the first write of a consumer to an entity table, to the audit tables or the read of the revocation floor fails with SQLSTATE 42501. RunConsumer makes it a transient refusal, and the consumed destination must land, so the message retries without end and holds back the later messages of its key. L1: a tick reads the tenant list once, so a tenant that is retired during a tick still gets a run. L2: a tick whose read of the tenant list fails ends with no observation. L3: when the last consumer is removed, no step takes back the grant of the worker role, and the schema manifest then reports a mismatch at each start. I7: the declaration does not refuse subject_from_identity: service_account, so a caller could have the subject of a worker; the runtime refuses that subject type for a person (authz.Person), but the declaration does not say so. Decision: (M1a) the step authorization_tables of the migration job holds the grants of the worker role in its one transaction, so no committed state lacks a grant that the running release needs (security re-review, M2): before the authorization text, it takes back from the worker role each privilege on each table and sequence of the runtime grants, on audit_event, audit_chain_heads and idempotency_keys, and gives the grants below; the authorization text then gives the worker role its column grants on the token of each protected table again; after it, the same for the revocation floor authz_floor, which that text makes. When the declaration has a consuming worker, it then gives the worker role SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE on the table of each entity that a consuming worker writes (no DELETE, as a worker declares no delete), INSERT on audit_event (no SELECT: the insert returns no row; security re-review, L4), SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE on audit_chain_heads, SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE on idempotency_keys and SELECT on authz_floor, and nothing more. Each table keeps its row-level security and its tenant policy for every role. The job refuses a consumer table that the runtime role gets no grant on. The schema manifest holds the grants of the worker role on each table whose grants it checks (idempotency_keys, authz_floor); the entity and audit tables have no grant check in the manifest yet. (M1b) A consumer run that fails with SQLSTATE 42501 is a permanent fault: RunConsumer returns a permanent refusal, so the outbox parks the message, and the generated handler sends worker.run.failed with the new outcome not_granted. (L1) RunWorker reads the tenant gate before tenant.Begin: a tenant that the gate holds as not active gets no run and is no failed run. (L2) A tick whose read of the tenant list fails sends the new built-in event worker.tick.failed with the worker name only, and logs the cause tenant_list_read with no error text. (L3) is the first half of M1a. (I7) The declaration refuses subject_from_identity: service_account under the rule no-bypass. Decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-15. The Product owner changes the design records that the file q141-design.json beside the notes of b-worker names: ST-SUP-RC35-OC06, ST-SUP-RC35-OC09, ST-SUP-RP10-LC18, ST-SUP-RP12-LC21, ST-SUP-RP14-LC03 and ST-DECL-INV24.

title: Should a start that a setting refused name the component and the variable in its failure record?
description: Found by the fourth walkthrough, 2026-11-15. A service with no DATABASE_URL, or with a database that it cannot reach, stops with the failure record Service failed, stage component[11].constructor[0]. ReadSettings already names the setting in its error, but the failure record holds no error text (ST-GEN-INV16), and ST-SUP-RP14-LC05 says that StartStage gives no stage for every failure that it does not list. So the operator cannot see which variable is missing. Options: (A) StartStage also gives service.start.setting.<component>.<variable> for a setting that ReadSettings refused, such as service.start.setting.postgres-adapter.DATABASE_URL, and service.start.database for a pool that did not open. Each stage comes from the fixed names of ST-SUP-RP14-LC01, so the record still holds a fixed stage and never a value or an error text. (B) The failure record gets a second field with the variable name. This changes the record format that the compiler generates, and every service gets new generated code. (C) No change: the operator runs stego env check before the start. Recommendation: (A). It changes only the runtime (a new runtime version, then the archetype pins), it keeps ST-GEN-INV16, and it names the cause at the place where the operator looks.
