The generated CLI sends a write again after a transport failure, an expired request or a 5xx answer only when its embedded OpenAPI document says that the service keeps the key of that write (ST-SUP-RC04-OC31). The document is fixed when the CLI is built. A CLI of an older or a newer release than the service can thus send a write again to an operation whose key the service does not keep, and the service can do the write two times. The cli-application README now says to build the CLI from the same release as the service (PR #456). A 5xx answer that the service writes rolls back the transaction, so a second request is safe there; the risk is an answer whose outcome is not known, such as a 503 after a lost connection at the commit, or a 502 or 504 of a proxy after the service committed. Prior art: draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header defines the request header and the 400, 409 and 422 answers, and no answer header; the Stripe API sends Idempotent-Replayed: true on an answer that it gives again from the store; the Stripe SDKs send a key with each POST and retry with it, because the Stripe API keeps the key of each POST. Options. (a) The answer header Idempotency-Kept: 1 on each answer, success or problem, that the service writes to a request with a key that it keeps, from a create and a patch of the idempotency component and from a command that takes the key. The CLI sends a write again after a 5xx answer only when that answer carries the header; after a transport failure or an expired request, which give no answer, it follows the document, as now; and it writes a warning to standard error when the document says that the service keeps the key and a 2xx answer has no header, which tells a CLI of another release. A 502 or 504 of a proxy has no header, so the CLI does not send it again and tells the caller that the write can be done. (b) The CLI reads the document of the running service (the discovery route, ST-SUP-RC20-OC53) before a write and compares it with its own document: one more request for each run, and no help when the document cannot be read. (c) The service refuses with 400 a key on a POST or PATCH operation that does not keep keys, so a CLI of another release fails at the first request, before it does a write: it changes the answer of ST-SUP-RC30-OC01 for each client that sends a key to each POST, which some HTTP clients do. (d) Keep the README rule only and close the item. Recommendation: (a), because it tells the truth of the service on each answer that the service writes, it costs no request, and a CLI of another release fails closed after a 5xx: it does not send a write again that the service may do two times. The changes of (a): the new output contracts ST-SUP-RC30-OC08 (idempotency component), ST-SUP-RC32-OC27 (command 1.16.0) and ST-SUP-RC04-OC34 (cli-application 1.13.0). The registry/components/cli-application README gets the header and the warning.

title: Does a command whose answer holds a google.protobuf.Any, Struct, Value or ListValue member make its generated CLI command Sensitive?
description: Found by the security review of PR #462 (sec-462, the residual of L1 and L4), 2026-11-19. A member that the proto file marks debug_redact is a secret: the OpenAPI document marks it x-sensitive, also at the root of a response that holds it at any depth (ST-SUP-RC20-OC54), and the generated CLI makes the command Sensitive, so the answer goes only to the file of --output-file (ST-SUP-RC04-OC33). A member of the type google.protobuf.Any, Struct, Value or ListValue has no fixed members: the fill can put any value in it at run time, such as an API key that a command makes, and no debug_redact mark reaches that value. The document gives such a member as an object with no fixed members, the same as google.protobuf.Empty, so the CLI cannot see it, and the command writes the answer to standard output. Options. (a) The rest-api component marks the root of a response schema x-stego-opaque true when the response message holds such a member at any depth, also deeper than the schema follows or past a recursive message; the CLI makes a command with that mark Sensitive, as for x-sensitive. The mark is for the CLI only: the service needs no key ring for it (ST-SUP-RP14-LC12), the member is not writeOnly, and the stored answers of the idempotency keys stay as now. A caller of such a command gives --output-file FILE. (b) As (a), and the runtime also treats the answer as a secret: it seals the stored answer and keys the fingerprint, so each service with such a command needs a key ring. This costs a key ring for each service that uses google.protobuf.Struct for plain data, such as labels or settings. (c) The CLI infers the type from the shape of the schema (an object with no fixed members, or additionalProperties true): no new mark, but google.protobuf.Empty, a recursive message cut at its depth and a map look the same, so the rule is not exact. (d) Keep the current rule and write in the README of the command component that a secret must be in a typed member with debug_redact, never in Any, Struct, Value or ListValue. The CLI then writes such a secret to standard output, a terminal or a log of a script. Recommendation: (a). It fails closed for the CLI, where the answer goes to a terminal or a log; it costs the caller only --output-file FILE; and it asks no key ring of a service that keeps plain data in google.protobuf.Struct. Prior art: the protobuf JSON form gives Any, Struct, Value and ListValue as arbitrary JSON (protojson), and the OpenAPI generators of grpc-gateway give google.protobuf.Struct as an object with additionalProperties, so no tool can see a secret in it. The changes of (a): ST-SUP-RC20-OC54 (rest-api 4.26.0) gets the x-stego-opaque mark, ST-SUP-RC04-OC33 (cli-application 1.18.0) gets the rule that the mark makes a command Sensitive, and ST-SUP-RP14-LC12 stays as it is. Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-19: the CLI makes such a command Sensitive; no key ring and no sealing for these types.

title: Does the answer of a query need the x-stego-opaque mark, and does a command over gRPC need the Idempotency-Kept metadata?
description: Found by the security review of PR #463 (sec-463, F5), 2026-11-19; written by the follow-up worker, run 27. First point. Decision ST-SUP-Q194 (a) marks the root of the response schema of a command x-stego-opaque when its message holds a google.protobuf.Any, Struct, Value or ListValue member, so the generated CLI makes the command Sensitive and writes its answer only to the file of --output-file (ST-SUP-RC20-OC54, ST-SUP-RC04-OC33). The OpenAPI document gives the answer of a get or list query as any JSON value, because the fill gives its form, so no mark reaches it, and the CLI writes each query answer to standard output. The query runtime gives a fill no secret field: the read-only value of an entity leaves out each field of sensitivity secret (ST-SUP-RC33-OC01), so a query answer holds a secret only when the fill makes one. Options. (a) Keep the rule: no mark on query answers. The docs of commands, queries and workers say that a query answer must not hold a secret, and that a call that makes a secret, such as an API key, is a command with a debug_redact member. (b) Mark the answer of each query x-stego-opaque, because its schema is any JSON value: the CLI then makes each query Sensitive, so each read needs --output-file, which removes the plain read from a terminal. (c) A query declaration gets a new setting sensitive: true, which marks its answer x-sensitive, so the CLI makes that query Sensitive; this adds a field to the declaration and to the query contract. Recommendation: (a). The runtime already keeps stored secrets out of each query fill, so only a fill that makes a secret can put one in a query answer, and that is the work of a command. Prior art: the protobuf JSON form and the OpenAPI generators of grpc-gateway give no mark for a value with no fixed members, so only the declaration can say that a value is secret. Second point. The answer Idempotency-Kept: 1 (ST-SUP-RC30-OC08, decision ST-SUP-Q193 (a)) is an HTTP header of the rest-api component. A command that the service serves over gRPC (ServeRPC) sends no such metadata, so a gRPC client cannot tell after a failure whether the service kept the key. The generated CLI and the SDKs call the HTTP routes only. Options. (d) Keep it for HTTP only, and say so in ST-SUP-RC30-OC08 and the README of the grpc-application component: a gRPC client resends a command after a failure only with the same key, which the idempotency store answers with the stored answer. (e) ServeRPC also sends the trailer metadata idempotency-kept: 1 under the same rule. Recommendation: (d), until a generated client calls a command over gRPC. Decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-19: (a) for query answers (no mark, a doc note) and (d) for gRPC (Idempotency-Kept is HTTP only).
